#1961. Tragic footballer Jesus de Miguel's devastated club Tenerife vow to financially support his one-year-old daughter until she turns 18 - as fundraiser passes £125,000

Published: 03:12 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 03:12 EST, 8 November 2026

Tenerife have committed to financially supporting the one-year-old baby daughter of Jesus de Miguel following the 30-year-old's tragic death this week.

De Miguel, 30, lost his life following a horror collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono in the latter stages of a second division game on the Spanish island.

The striker's girlfriend, Maria Fernandez, and their daughter, Carla, witnessed the incident from the stands. A post-mortem found De Miguel died from 'accidental chest trauma'. It is described in the preliminary report as a 'cause consistent with the player's death'.

The footballing world came together in Tenerife on Thursday for the 30-year-old's funeral, with De Miguel's team-mates, Spain national team coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez offering support to his devastated family – who said his passing has left an 'impossible void to fill'.

And now Tenerife have confirmed they will support De Miguel's family and Carla following their loss.

Club CEO Antonio Manuel Porro Granados told The Athletic: 'Our plan is to stand by the girl and make sure the entire Tenerife family supports her. We want to be there for her at least until she reaches adulthood.

Tenerife have vowed to support Jesus De Miguel's one-year-old daughter following his death

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel was struck by Jesus Owono during a second division contest and lost his life

'This is a commitment we have made at the initiative of our majority shareholder, Rayco Garcia, and one that we all fully support. It is a commitment that Tenerife, as a club, is making to the family and to their daughter, Carla.

'We will provide the maximum possible support in every respect, beyond what we are legally obliged to provide. We are also exploring other ways of increasing the financial support, so that, at least in material terms, the circumstances do not affect their lives quite so much — although, of course, it is impossible for them not to have an impact.'

Tenerife's commitment follows the development that a fundraiser for the family has passed £125,000 in donations. Spanish footballers Alvaro Morata and Alex Baena are among those who have pledged to the crowdfunding campaign.

De Miguel's family are also reportedly set to receive around £300,000 in base compensation following his death.

Goalkeeper Owono has shut down his Instagram account and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash he has received – which saw him subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans as he left the pitch.

On Wednesday, he issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Tenerife say they will financially support the family, while a fundraiser has amassed more than £125,000 in donations

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged on Tuesday that homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

#1957. Premier League star's career criminal brother beats Home Office bid to deport him to Africa - as he awaits trial for kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery

Published: 03:45 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 8 November 2026

The street criminal brother of a Premier League star has beaten a Home Office attempt to deport him to Africa - by citing his own human rights.

The gang member and aspiring rapper, now in his twenties, was the subject of a concerted four year attempt by the government to send him to his family's country of origin in West Africa because of his shocking criminal record.

The young man, who has never held down a job, is currently in prison for dangerous driving and carrying a knife - while awaiting yet another court case accused of kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery.

During his teens he had played academy football for several Premier League teams but while his brother went on to make it and is now a multi-millionaire, the man instead got sucked into street crime.

And he has been involved in so much anti-social and criminal behaviour since then that he has even incurred a number of gunshot wounds.

But the wannabe rapper has managed to win a long-running deportation bid by the Home Office to kick him out of Britain as an undesirable - arguing that this wouldn't be fair as all his significant ties are here.

A Premier League footballer - who cannot be named for legal reasons - has seen his career criminal brother living in Britian beat a Home Office attempt to deport him back to West Africa

The Home Office first targeted him for deportation in 2022 after he was sentenced to 20 months in jail having been caught with a sword in his waistband, which in turn meant had breached an existing order about his criminal behaviour.

They lost that attempt to get him out of Britain but appealed - and have now lost that appeal too.

The gang member is 'healthy and capable' according to a judge but has never worked - in stark contrast to his hugely successful brother, a full international footballer who has made countless top flight appearances.

A court heard the foreign national has a 'sustained history of criminal offending involving repeated breaches of Criminal Behaviour Orders, possession of offensive weapons, breaches of licence conditions, recalls to custody, and recent charges. He has a history of offending with knives since the age of 17'.

Totaling his various jail terms together he has spent three of the last eight years prison.

But despite his ongoing recurrent criminality, the Home Office has failed in its latest attempt to deport him after a judge ruled he is 'socially and culturally integrated' into the UK and a return to his home country would leave him 'very much an outsider'.

The immigration tribunal decided he would face 'very significant obstacles to integration' in his home country and prevented the government from deporting him by ruling it would breach his human rights.

That decision came despite it emerging that he has an uncle in the country and grew up with a familiarity of the country, including its culture and food, while his mother maintains links to the country and visited as recently as 2024.

But the judge said the 'significance of these ties should not be exaggerated' because he has never been there.

They said his social and cultural identity 'has been almost entirely formed in the UK and by British culture' - even though he was born overseas and his family come from West Africa. The Home Office is appealing the decision and so the brother could still face deporation.

The knife criminal first arrived in the UK in 2006 after being born in another country where he doesn't have nationality.

He is in a relationship with a British woman with whom he shares a baby.

Their child was born in February but the rapper has only met them twice because he remains incarcerated.

There is no evidence that having a partner or child has reformed his criminal ways, a court heard.

The Home Office argued he is a healthy young adult capable of work who has a familiarity with the culture of his home country and has family ties in the country who could provide guidance and support.

But the judge concluded it would breach his human rights because he has never lived or visited and would be an outsider if returned.

#1956. Thibaut Courtois reveals how Jose Mourinho has changed since Chelsea

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 16:14

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois has revealed that Jose Mourinho is a calmer and less intense manager than the one he worked under at Chelsea 12 years ago, although the Portuguese coach has lost none of his commanding personality.

The Belgium international, who won the Premier League under Mourinho at Stamford Bridge in 2014-15, has been reunited with his former manager following the latter's return to the Santiago Bernabeu during the summer.

Their second spell together has allowed Courtois to observe how Mourinho's approach to managing players has evolved, particularly in the dressing room.

Speaking to Sky Sports during the Web Summit in Lisbon, the 34-year-old suggested that experience has made the former Chelsea boss more measured in his dealings with players.

However, Courtois believes Mourinho's authority remains unmistakable and even suggested that his arrival provided precisely the kind of presence Real Madrid needed.

The goalkeeper also shared an unusual story about their reunion, revealing that he accidentally ignored Mourinho's first message for two weeks while representing Belgium at the 2026 World Cup.

“I think sometimes he’s a bit more calmer” Thibaut Courtois on Jose Mourinho's managerial style at Real Madrid compared to how he was at Chelsea ⏪ https://t.co/9HGnNSTzE2

Courtois was part of the Chelsea squad that secured the Premier League title during Mourinho's second spell in west London, having returned from his loan spell at Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2014.

The pair worked together during a successful 2014-15 campaign, when Chelsea also won the League Cup, before Mourinho left the club in December 2015.

More than a decade later, Courtois believes the Portuguese coach has developed a slightly different approach to handling the demands of an elite dressing room.

"I think he himself says he has maybe grown to be more mature," Courtois explained.

"And with the experience, I think sometimes he is a bit calmer.

"At Chelsea, I remember he was a bit stronger in the dressing room, a bit more intense. Also now he is, but I feel he is a tiny bit less from what I remember from 12 years ago."

The Belgian nevertheless stressed that Mourinho continues to command the attention of everyone around him.

"But he's still the same personality, the same presence," he added.

"He fills the room. When you come in and he's there, you feel he's there. I think that is something that we needed."

Those comments offer an insight into how Mourinho has been received by one of Madrid's most experienced players following his return to the Spanish capital.

The 63-year-old began his second spell at the Bernabeu after Madrid endured a trophyless 2025-26 campaign, with Courtois among the senior figures already familiar with his methods.

Mourinho's side have recovered from two early La Liga defeats to establish an eight-match winning streak across all competitions.

That sequence includes a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at Camp Nou on October 25 and last weekend's 3-0 success against Valencia.

Madrid have also won their opening four Champions League matches, leaving them well placed to secure direct qualification for the knockout stages.

In La Liga, they sit three points behind leaders Barcelona after 12 matches, having accumulated 30 points from 10 victories.

Despite his enthusiasm about working with Mourinho again, Courtois admitted their reunion began with a communication mishap.

The goalkeeper was away with Belgium at the World Cup when Mourinho first attempted to contact him following his appointment at Real Madrid.

However, the message arrived while Courtois was travelling, and he failed to notice it amid the disruption caused by the flight and the time difference.

"He texted me when he arrived in Madrid, but I ignored his message for two weeks," Courtois revealed.

"We were at the World Cup at the time, and the day he texted me, we were on a plane."

The Belgian explained that the lack of Wi-Fi meant several messages went unnoticed, with the misunderstanding only becoming clear when Mourinho contacted him again after an international match.

"Later, after a match, he texted me again, and I asked someone at Real Madrid, 'Is this the coach's number?' But everything is fine now."

The incident did nothing to diminish Courtois's enthusiasm about their reunion.

The goalkeeper explained that he and Mourinho had parted on good terms when the manager left Chelsea and that he had been looking forward to working under him again.

For Courtois, the most significant change is not in Mourinho's authority but in how he exercises it.

That assessment comes at an encouraging moment for Madrid, who will attempt to extend their winning sequence when they host Celta Vigo on November 21 following the international break.

The reunion has already produced positive results, and Courtois's account suggests that Mourinho has found a balance between the demanding management style that defined his Chelsea years and a more measured approach at the Bernabeu.

“I think we lack time in the final third of the pitch. We control the ball away from the opponent’s area. This is also a key point for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault. Pulisic is away from the area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area.

“All these players play far from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

#1954. JJ Gabriel to Real Madrid: Announcement 'imminent' as Los Blancos win race for Man United wonderkid

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 16:20, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 16:22

JJ Gabriel will reportedly sign his contract with Real Madrid by the start of next week, with Los Blancos winning the race for the Manchester United wonderkid.

Man United were stunned in September when the attacker's representatives told the English club that he wanted to leave in search of pastures new.

The teenager had been due to sign scholarship terms with the Red Devils on his 16th birthday in October, with a professional contract then expected to follow a year later.

Man United had allegedly initially been confident of convincing JJ Gabriel to remain at Old Trafford, but the club have since admitted defeat.

Barcelona, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain had all been linked with the attacker, but Real Madrid have won the race for his signature.

According to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos, JJ Gabriel is due to sign his contract with Real Madrid by next week at the latest.

As a result, the saga is set to come to an end in the near future.

Real Madrid allegedly want to initially use JJ Gabriel in their Castilla outfit, who operate in Spain's third division, but it is not expected to be long before the teenager secures first-team action in either La Liga or the Champions League.

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, and he is regarded as one of the brightest young talents in world football.

The forward has a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the campaign, but the teenager has a European passport through both of his parents.

A FIFA loophole could therefore see him join Real Madrid at the start of 2027.

JJ Gabriel, who has not been at Man United's training complex since September, boasts a record of 29 goals and four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s.

#1953. Ryan Porteous on his Scotland exile, Steve Clarke relationship and ‘things that people don’t see’

When the goal that clinched Scotland’s World Cup return went in, Ryan Porteous might once have hoped he’d be celebrating with his Scottish teammates.

Instead, he was thousands of miles away at what he terms a “practice facility” in California. Jumping on top of him were not Scotland international teammates but those from Los Angeles FC. “When Kenny McLean scored (against Denmark) from the halfway line, I’ve got half the team in LA shouting and screaming for Scotland!” the defender recalled. “It was brilliant."

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Due to the time difference, he was able to sit and watch most of the qualifiers after training. “Obviously being in the mode of being a fan is only good up to a point," he noted. "You want to be involved, so I’m delighted to be back again.”

Porteous has played just one minute plus injury time for the national team – against Greece last year – since being sent off in the first half of the opening match of Euro 2024 against Germany.

The received wisdom is he was being punished for his rash, penalty-conceding challenge on Ilkay Gundogan in Munich, with Scotland already 2-0 down. The roof subsequently caved in and Scotland were beaten 5-1.

The pitiful sight of Porteous waiting for the trap door to open at the Allianz Arena - there is a hatch leading to the underground players’ tunnel - after he was given his marching orders is still burned in the mind. For him as much as anyone.

The first surprise on seeing him again is his lack of bitterness towards Steve Clarke, the manager who initially handed him his chance before seemingly ghosting him. In actual fact they continued to enjoy a healthy relationship and were in contact throughout the time he was being overlooked.

“That happens in football, it’s just one of those things,” Porteous reflected. “I’ve had a career where I’m up and down, I’m left and right, you just need to bounce back from it.

“But it was a fantastic experience for me to be part of that run we went on. It helped me grow massively.

“I don’t look at it as being unfair. Me and the old gaffer (Clarke) spoke regularly. We had loads of conversations, both when I was in and out of the squad. Those are the things that people obviously don’t see.

“They maybe think Steve Clarke is the type of person who wouldn’t phone you or text you. But he did. We spoke loads to be honest. He was really honest with me.

"I texted him when he left the role and he messaged back eager to see me get back in the squad. Everyone knows Steve is a manager who, if he picks a squad and they do well for them and they get to a tournament, he’s loyal.”

Porteous perhaps didn’t help himself. Clarke finally played him again against Greece in a Nations League play-off in March last year with Scotland desperately defending a 1-0 lead given to them by Scott McTominay’s first-half penalty. Sent on after 89 minutes to replace Anthony Ralston, he could realistically have seen red once more with a clumsy challenge.

He wasn’t picked again by Clarke although he was placed on stand-by for the World Cup. Already in the States, having joined LAFC from Watford, he would have made for a handy replacement.

In the event he wasn’t required. He still flew cross country to Boston to join in the fun when his schedule – the Major League Soccer season had only paused for the World Cup - allowed. He didn’t have tickets but he did at least taste the Tartan Army invasion of Fenway Park, home of the Boston Red Sox. “I had a few days off at one point and I went out to Boston,” he recalled. "I didn’t manage to go to the games, but I saw my friends and family who were over and went to the baseball as well. Being in that fan environment, it just gives you that extra little bit of hunger to get back.”

And now he is back, at the behest of new manager Sebastien Pocognoli rather than Clarke. Porteous, who was in action as recently as Sunday in the 2-1 loss to Seattle Sounders, has replaced the injured Stephen Welsh. He has been joined by fellow late call-up David Bates, who returns from an even longer exile of seven years following an injury to Luis Binks.

The delight is written across Porteous’ tanned face. “It’s very hot (out there),” he says. “They are actually choking for a bit of rain just now.”

He jokes that he might just be the first person ever to move from Dalkeith, where he grew up and stayed while with Hibs, to LA. There were stop-offs at the equally unprepossessing Watford and Preston, where he was on loan, in between times.

Even the accent has had a glow-up. “I’ve had to change it so that people can understand me over there,” he said. “For the first couple of months, everyone was asking me to repeat myself.”

One thing hasn’t changed. He laments that he is still losing his hair. “I used to blame the wind at East Mains (Hibs’ training ground) for losing my hair, but it’s still falling out over in LA even without the wind!” he smiled.

He hopes the fans will recognise his old qualities minus the impetuousness that has bedevilled his performances in the past, stretching back to his time at Hibs. It’s still slightly surreal to see him listed in the same team as Son Heung-min, who left Spurs to join LAFC for an MLS record fee of £20 million two summers ago.

“Son is brilliant,” he said. “Some high-profile guys like him maybe get a reputation for going to America and taking it easy.

“But he has been unbelievable. He plays basically every single game and gives absolutely 100 per cent. He’s one of the best in every game and every training session. He’s a really top, top guy as well.”

#1952. MN: Hostile welcome, Amorim’s avoidance, De Rossi’s praise – behind the scenes of the win in Genoa

Some of the unseen details from AC Milan’s win away against Genoa have emerged, ranging from hostility to strong praise.

Goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes would be enough for Milan, who were nonetheless left clinging on in the final stages after Ellertsson’s goal. MilanNews have revealed some of the behind-the-scenes moments from the Marassi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The day in Genoa wasn’t exactly a walk in the park. First and foremost, there was the rather hostile atmosphere created by the Genoa fans towards the Rossoneri. This forced the relevant authorities to ban all residents of Lombardy from attending.

Milan fan groups weren’t even allowed to go to the Aquarium in Genoa’s Porto Antico. It is a shame for so many reasons, and one that reflects the complicated state under which Italian football still operates.

However, there were still Milanisti there to support the team and they made their voices heard. At the end of the match, both Goncalo Ramos and Diego Moreira gave their shirts to young fans in the away sector.

The game could have been a totally different story had it not been for Davide Massa’s controversial decision. At start of the second half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball, was racing alone toward the penalty area with Cisse to his left, and was fouled by Marcandalli.

Despite the fact it was a clear last-man challenge, he was not sent off. When asked Amorim about yesterday’s specific incident and the refereeing method in general in the press conference, the Portuguese coach responded with a laugh, a smile and a grimace.

It was as if to say: “I’d like to say something, but it’s better if I don’t.” His public response went along this path: “I won’t comment on it, you have the match, because I know that talking about referees isn’t something that could help my team. I just want to help my team, so I won’t say anything about the referees.”

Speaking of press conferences, Daniele De Rossi’s thoughts on Amorim and Modric were very interesting: “I shouldn’t judge Amorim. He’s younger than me, but he has a lot more experience than me. I learn from him. We study him, we watch him. He plays with a system that I really like.

“He puts a lot of quality on the wings, something I’ve also tried to do here. Certainly not Moreira, but with the right proportions and possibilities. I like the way he communicates; he doesn’t blame his players even when he loses, he’s always honest when he loses. He’s doing a great job.

“For anyone who loves this sport, it’s exciting to see Modric play football like this at 41. Last year I had him man-marked, this year he played with two. He has more playing time. Maybe he plays a little slower, but the idea is there.

“We clashed a couple of times and I told him, ‘I don’t play anymore so I can’t beat you up.’ But he’s great, really great. He’s like Rabiot: world-class players. Really beautiful.”

#1951. Michael Carrick reveals club bosses have not told him if he will still have a job next week, with Man United languishing in relegation zone ahead of Aston Villa clash

Published: 17:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 04:50 EST, 8 November 2026

Michael Carrick has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone.

United bosses handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in 10 games.

United slipped into the bottom three after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City on Saturday, and could be in last place by the time they kick off against Villa depending on the outcome of other games involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The situation could leave Carrick's position under threat during the two-week international break. Asked if he has been told outright that he will be in charge next week, the United boss replied: 'No. Just carry on as absolute normal.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night.

Michael Carrick revealed that club chiefs have not told him if he'll be in charge next week

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), Omar Berrada (centre) and Jason Wilcox (right) have not informed their manager about their plans for the international break

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

#1949. Netherlands vs Greece - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 11 Nov 2026 16:28, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 19:37

Potentially deciding who takes top spot in Group 2, the Netherlands and Greece will meet in Amsterdam for a UEFA Nations League clash on Friday evening.

Both unbeaten after four games - and level on eight points apiece - the sides are set to convene for their penultimate League A fixture.

With two rounds remaining, the fight for a qualification from Group 2 remains close, with the Netherlands and Greece only separated by goals scored - in that respect, the Greeks trail by two.

Meanwhile, traditional heavyweights Germany sit just three points behind in third place, and only the top two will go through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So far, the Netherlands have won twice and twice fought back to draw, showing plenty of character under new national coach Xavi.

Cody Gakpo's late strike stole a point against old foes Germany on matchday one, before home and away wins over rock-bottom Serbia were split by a thrilling game in Greece.

Trailing 2-0 as the final half-hour approached, Oranje roared back to claim a draw, thanks to goals from captain Virgil van Dijk and impact substitute Tijjani Reijnders.

All of which means three points from Friday's reverse fixture could see them potentially confirm entry to the knockout phase, which will begin early next year.

That 2-2 draw in Thessaloniki was as close as Greece have come to beating their Dutch counterparts in a senior competitive match.

Extending a long reign of dominance, the Netherlands had previously won both qualifiers between the pair en route to Euro 2024, but the Greeks will be buoyed by their meeting on matchday three.

Only promoted from League B last time around, the Galanolefki are still undefeated at Europe's elite level, as a talented new generation breaks through.

After overturning a deficit to beat Serbia in their opener - via a stoppage-time winner from Como striker Tasos Douvikas - they followed up with an impressive 1-0 win over Germany.

Having subsequently come within minutes of upsetting the Netherlands, three days later they held Jurgen Klopp and co to a goalless home draw.

Firmly in contention for a quarter-final berth, Ivan Jovanovic's side will now aim to build on that momentum with an historic success at Johan Cruijff Arena.

The hosts must negotiate their final pair of group games without Ryan Gravenberch, Kenneth Taylor, Brian Brobbey and Van Dijk, all of whom have withdrawn due to injury.

Brentford's Sepp van den Berg has been drafted in as cover for Oranje's vastly experienced skipper, who received his 100th international cap last month.

Juventus midfielder Teun Koopmeiners partnered Van Dijk against Serbia, but the more conventional North London duo of Jan Paul van Hecke and Jurrien Timber are likely to play on Friday night.

Mexx Meerdink impressed in Xavi's first camp, yet Donyell Malen will expect to start after returning to the squad, having scored 14 goals in 12 Roma appearances this season.

Another Serie A star, Douvikas recently netted a Champions League hat-trick; however, he faces a fight to displace Vangelis Pavlidis or Fotis Ioannidis in the visitors' front line.

In fact, Jovanovic has plenty of attacking options to choose from, including Konstantinos Karetsas and Premier League pair Christos Tzolis and Charalampos Kostoulas.

After picking up their second booking of the campaign against Germany, both Christos Zafeiris and Manolis Saliakas must serve a one-match ban; the latter's absence offers a chance for Lazaros Rota or Georgios Vagiannidis to start at right-back.

Verbruggen; Dumfries, J. Timber, Van Hecke, Van de Ven; Q. Timber, De Jong, Veerman; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo

Tzolakis; Vagiannidis, Mavropanos, Koulierakis, Tsimikas; Masouras, Kourbelis, Androutsos, Tzolis; Ionannidis, Pavlidis

As the Netherlands can be caught out at the back - and their visitors have a bright crop of attacking talent - there should be more goals, after the teams' entertaining contest last month.

Though Greece are a rising force, their unbeaten streak could come to an end, as Xavi can welcome back Malen and Frenkie de Jong - even if his injured captain will be missed.

Fabian Hurzeler's men are five points adrift of leaders Arsenal and one ahead of third placed Manchester City.

Brighton are also the leading scorers in the division with 26 goals and have conceded just seven times - only Arsenal have leaked fewer with five.

"There is an argument to be made that they would be the nearest pursuers to Arsenal," said Goodman, speaking to Betway.

"For Brighton to be able to sustain it through a 38-game Premier League season and a European campaign, you kind of think maybe not win the league, but absolutely, you hope that they can be challenging for a top-four Champions League spot."

Goodman, who had a prolific career as a striker for the likes of West Bromwich Albion, Sunderland and Wolves, has been impressed by the rise of Brighton and believes it’s just reward for how the club operates and long-term planning.

“I’ve been commentating for Sky Sports for 20 years next March, and I’ve commentated on Brighton and Hove Albion in League One and a lot in the Championship over that period of time,” Goodman added.

“To see the progression of the football club, along with others like Bournemouth and Brentford who are very similar in terms of the trajectory is wonderful and highlights the benefit of being a forward-thinking, well-run football club that plans ahead.

“It is wonderful to watch football clubs progress, and I think that over the last certainly few seasons since the Europa Conference League has been introduced by UEFA, it has certainly provided a happy hunting ground for Premier League clubs in terms of being able to win it.

“And there’s no reason whatsoever that Brighton cannot go on to win the Europa Conference League.

Mauricio Pochettino, who is in charge of the United States, is set to be appointed as the club's new head coach once Carrick's exit has been confirmed.

Earlier this month, Emery revealed that discussions were taking place over keeping him at Villa Park on an even longer basis.

"My ambition is to keep our consistency and how we are improving and building lots of things positively. It is a huge challenge," the Villa boss told reporters.

"They decided, speaking with us last year, to build a new stand to add more supporters at Villa Park. That is a clear step forward to get better.

"How we are increasing our budget each year, and revenue through our performance by playing in Europe and improving players, selling players, then buying young talented players, this is the process and ambition we should keep in the future.

"I had a good meeting with Nassef Sawiris, very good meeting, very positive. Let's talk next week, trying to get everything we spoke about together. We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a deal, yes."

Man United faced Villa in the Premier League last time out, twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Emery's side at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils will return to action against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22, and the expectation is that Pochettino will be in charge for that contest.

Earps, 33, was a hero of England's Euro 2022 victory at Wembley and starred at the World Cup in 2023, saving a penalty in the final. She won BBC Sports Personality of the Year but later lost her England place to rival Hannah Hampton and retired in acrimonious circumstances.

'Welcome to the world, Xander,' she posted on Instagram, with a photograph of her newborn's hand.

In a video released on Friday, Earps said: 'I've been keeping a little secret from you all. And I don't think I can talk my way out of this one. So, I think I'm going to have to show you.

'I can't quite believe I'm writing this, but yesterday Kitty and I welcomed our beautiful baby boy into the world!

Mary Earps has revealed the name of her baby boy following his secret birth: Xander

Earps and her partner Kitty (second right) revealed news of welcoming a baby boy (YouTube/Mary Earps)

#1942. Manchester United face £900m Adidas deal threat amid relegation fears

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 17:14

Manchester United's worsening Premier League campaign could have significant financial consequences, with a relegation clause in their £900m Adidas contract allowing the sportswear manufacturer to halve its annual payments to the club.

Michael Carrick's side have entered the November international break in the relegation zone, sitting 18th with just eight points from their opening 10 league matches.

United have won only once in the Premier League this season and are without a victory in their last eight top-flight fixtures, equalling their longest winless run in the competition's history.

Sunday's extraordinary 4-4 draw with Aston Villa offered some relief after two stoppage-time goals rescued a point at Old Trafford, but the result did little to improve their precarious league position.

Their struggles have brought renewed attention to the commercial implications of a potential drop into the Championship, with the club's latest financial disclosures confirming a provision that could substantially reduce one of their most lucrative revenue streams.

Although relegation remains a hypothetical outcome with much of the season still to play, United's Adidas agreement includes both a payment reduction mechanism and a potential termination clause.

United agreed a 10-year extension to their partnership with Adidas in July 2023, taking their relationship with the German sportswear company through to June 2035.

The extension carries a minimum guarantee of £900m, in addition to the £750m guaranteed under the original agreement, bringing the total contractual guarantee across the extended partnership to £1.65bn, subject to adjustments.

However, the club's annual report for the financial year ending June 30, 2026 confirms that those payments are not entirely protected against a decline in sporting fortunes.

Under the agreement, Adidas has the right to reduce the applicable payments for any year by 50% if United's men's first team are not competing in the Premier League.

Crucially, that would be a reduction in the relevant annual payment, rather than an automatic loss of £900m.

The agreement also gives Adidas the option of terminating its partnership by providing one full season's notice if United are relegated from the Premier League or are otherwise excluded from England's top division.

That provision does not mean a termination would automatically follow relegation, but it would give the manufacturer a contractual route to end the relationship.

United's financial disclosures also confirm a separate penalty for failing to qualify for the Champions League.

From the 2025-26 season onwards, their agreement includes a £10m deduction for each campaign in which the men's team do not participate in Europe's premier club competition.

The club's failure to qualify for the 2025-26 Champions League already triggered one such deduction.

These clauses illustrate how United's commercial income is linked to their performances on the pitch, even under a long-term agreement with one of the world's biggest sportswear brands.

The relegation provision would only become relevant if the club actually dropped out of the Premier League, but their current position has made a previously remote contractual scenario worthy of attention.

United have not played outside England's top flight since the 1974-75 campaign, when they immediately secured promotion from the Second Division.

Their last relegation came in 1974, six years after winning the European Cup under Sir Matt Busby.

They have never been relegated during the Premier League era, which began in 1992, although their 15th-place finish in 2024-25 represented their worst final position since the competition's formation.

The current campaign has produced an even more alarming start.

United's position after 10 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when Ron Atkinson was replaced by Sir Alex Ferguson in November 1986.

Ferguson eventually guided United to an 11th-place finish that season, before overseeing a transformation that delivered 13 Premier League titles.

Carrick now faces a very different challenge, with his side having conceded 19 league goals and secured only one win from their first 10 fixtures.

The latest setback came against Aston Villa, when United recovered from two goals down on two separate occasions before Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time.

Their resilience earned a point, but defensive mistakes continued to undermine the team.

Carrick acknowledged afterwards that United had been making matches unnecessarily difficult through avoidable errors, while insisting that their overall performance deserved more than a draw.

The Red Devils will return from the international break with a trip to Liverpool on November 22, a fixture that presents another difficult test of their attempts to climb away from the bottom three.

For now, there is no suggestion that Adidas has taken action over United's league position. The contractual consequences would depend on their final status at the end of the season.

Nevertheless, the club's financial filings establish precisely what could be at stake should their worst start in four decades eventually result in an unprecedented Premier League relegation.

Celta Vigo will aim to avoid a shock elimination in the first round of the Copa del Rey when they tackle fourth-tier outfit Salamanca CF UDS on Friday night.

The visitors have been runners-up in the Copa del Rey on three previous occasions, including in 2000-01, while Salamanca have never been past the second round of the tournament.

Salamanca are managed by a legendary figure in La Liga, with ex-Athletic Bilbao forward Iker Muniain at the helm of the Spanish outfit.

Salamanca have been a fourth-tier outfit since 2024-25, earning promotion from the fifth tier in 2023-24, and they are aiming to reach the second round of the Copa del Rey for just the second time in their history, previously securing a spot at that stage in 2024-25.

The hosts will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Real Avila in the league, and they also recorded a 1-0 victory in their last home fixture over Gimnastia Segoviana on November 1.

This fixture had originally been due to take place at the end of October, but it was postponed following the tragic train crash in the province of Toledo, and it was then agreed by both clubs to be played during the international break.

Celta will enter this match off the back of a goalless draw with Levante; the result left them 11th in the La Liga table, picking up 13 points from 12 matches.

#1936. ‘Able to build relationships’ – Steyning Town boss O’Neill says settled team is bringing results

The Barrowmen struggled for form early in their return to the Isthmian South East – but they are now up to 15th.

The Barrowmen won only one of their first five – but after a run of four straight league losses, they’ve won three of their past four – most recently Saturday’s 2-1 home win over Horley courtesy of Leo Ginger and Charlie Pitcher’s goals.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

O’Neill said: “The season so far has been really positive, although frustrating at times. Through August and September, up to the start of October, we had a lot of injuries and players away.

"We had no real continuity within any unit, but since we’ve been able to build relationships over the past six or seven weeks, things have started to come together.

"We’ve started to see some results, which is a reflection of the hard work the boys have been putting in. So it’s been difficult at times but we’ve managed to make it work and we’ve put a good group together.”

O’Neill said the highlights so far had been two down-to-the-wire wins. "One was at home to Faversham – we were 2-0 up, then it was 2-2 and we scored to make it 3-2 in the 90th minute, which was amazing.

"And then Herne Bay away, we were 2-0 up, it went to 3-3 and we scored with the last kick to win it. Those have probably been our best two wins.

"In terms of performances, our first away, away to Eastbourne Town, it wasn’t the nicest or the prettiest, but to get a clean sheet and defend the goal and our lead was excellent.

"Saturday’s win versus Horley was frustrating because we got caught up in a game that suited them. We started really well but got sucked into it.

"We had to work hard on Saturday and knew we would have to – Horley are fighting for every point, they’re fighting every battle so it was important we matched that.

"The squad is looking really good now. We’ve had a lot of injuries and suspensions but Saturday I think we only have one injury and one suspension so we have 16 players to choose from which is nice – against Horley last weekend we only had 13 available.

"We have a couple of additions coming in this week and hopefully they will boost us over the next eight weeks. But to come out of seven weeks of Saturday-Tuesday games and be where we are, we’re really positive.

“We can recover properly between games now from Saturday to Saturday so that’s positive and hopefully we’ll see a reflection of that in how we play and in getting more points on the board.”

O’Neill’s men visit leaders Hastings on Saturday – the Pilot Field men are second in the table although have lost their past three home games.

#1935. Andy Robertson: My 102 caps is a chance to recognise what Sir Kenny Dalglish did - not me

Scotland captain Andy Robertson claims his 102nd cap should be a reason to celebrate Sir Kenny Dalglish and not himself as he prepares to join his fellow former Liverpool player as record appearance holder.

The 32-year-old will draw level with Dalglish when he leads Scotland out at Hampden on Friday against North Macedonia in the Nations League.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“Tomorrow’s not really about me,” the Tottenham left-back said. “It’s about him in my opinion. For how long the record stood, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is.

“It’s another reason for our country to tip our hat to one of the greatest players that have played the game, never mind in Scotland, he’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.”

Robertson was speaking on the 40th anniversary of Dalglish’s final international, a 3-0 win over Luxembourg when he was in his second season as Liverpool player/manager.

“That tells you everything that you need to know, the fact that he’s juggling all that and still showing up for his country,” Robertson said. “He reminds me all the time that 102 caps back then was a lot harder than 102 caps now, and he’s right because there were less games.

“In terms of numbers, I’ll stand side by side with him, but I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been for our country. He was arguably the best player in the world at his time and he’ll always be the greatest in this country.”

Dalglish recently joked that he hoped Robertson would retire before he sets a new record. “We’ve had a lot of jokes, but I also know deep down how proud he is of me and how happy he is for me as well,” the former Dundee United player said. “I always remember when I got the captaincy, he was one of the first people to text me and say, ‘I know I’ve been out of the game maybe a little bit, but if you need help, if you need somebody to bounce anything off, then I can be that person’.

“To have somebody like that, that you can bounce anything off and rely on, him and his family have been such a massive help to my family, especially in my time at Liverpool.

“I’ve got no doubt there’ll be a couple of texts that will get exchanged. I know we laugh and we joke, publicly and privately, but I know he’s proud of me and he’s happy for what I’ve achieved as well.”

Robertson is set to surpass Dalglish in Switzerland on Monday and he is no mood to slow down. “I’m still hungry to achieve more for the country,” he said. “I want to get Scotland back to another major tournament, I want to try and get out the group stages.

“Secondly, I want to try and leave the squad in the best possible place in terms of the quality coming through, the characters they’ve got, the mentality they’ve got.

“If I can leave that behind, then I can maybe enjoy Scotland games a bit more and I can join the fans and party with them.”

#1933. Chichester City blow hot and cold – but keep on battling

On Saturday goals from Harry Bridle and Lucas Pattenden earned a creditable 2-1 home win over Bath City, who had a man sent off just before the break. See David Richardson’s Chi City v Bath City gallery here.

But on Tuesday night at Chertsey, Ben Pashley’s goal just after the hour came when City were already 2-0 down and they couldn’t go on to rescue a point.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three points from six have left City seventh, having won nine of their opening 17 games.

City now take a break from league action for a week. They visit National League South high flyers Salisbury in the second round of the FA Trophy on Saturday, then go to SCFL Premier side Hassocks in the third round of the Sussex Transport Senior Cup on Tuesday.

Manager Miles Rutherford said they were delighted to beat Bath – but frustrated not to get anything from the Chertsey trip.

“We’re still blowing hot and cold, but I think it’s the same for a lot of clubs in this league. Anyone can beat anyone, you’re seeing that in results,” Rutherford said.

“It was a good win on Saturday and Chertsey was a fairly even game. We were 1-0 down at half-time but should have been 2-1 up – we missed two glorious chances.

“We felt confident at half-time but started the second half poorly. When we did get one back we didn’t really build on it.”

Coach Darin Killpartrick said: “I felt we deserved to beat Bath. Their red card changed things but it was another excellent, entertaining game with two sides going at each other.

“At Chertsey, the effort from the players was excellent but on the technical side, we failed in some aspects.”

Rutherford admitted the current schedule was testing City’s small squad, with a number of players now injured – including Curtis da Costa, Ryan Davidson and James Sweet.

He said they’d go to Salisbury for Saturday’s Trophy tie as underdogs but determined to give it their best shot.

“We’re having to do a lot of travelling at the moment but we have to get on with it and try to grind out some results.”

Killpartrick said: “It feels like a pinch point of the season at the moment. We’ll get through it but we need all the support we can get.

“We had more than 600 at Oaklands Park for the Bath City and would love local people to keep coming and helping us grow the support. And we wouldn’t mind a nice coach for away trips if anyone wants to help!”

Here is Ian Worden’s match report from the defeat at Chertsey….

Chichester City might have been the better side but came away from Surrey with nothing from Chertsey Town.

Nathan Minhas scored on seven minutes after Will Sweet under-hit a back header to keeper Max Evans, and Daniel Berry made it 2-0 in the second half. Ben Pashley pulled one back for Chi on 63 for what would prove to be a consolation goal.

City made two changes to the starting XI which beat Bath City on Saturday. Skipper Rob Hutchings once again lined up at left back with Isaac Bello on the other side, partnering Pashley and Sweet, this time, in the centre of defence. Evans began as usual between the posts with Joe Moore, Emmett Dunn, Lucas Pattenden and Lloyd Rowlatt, given a start, in midfield behind top scorer Harry Bridle up front and Brandon Chebby who scored twice against Frome and earned the MoM award versus the other Somerset club at the weekend.

Moore cleared in the fourth minute of play and Evans collected a forward pass from Darryl Harrison as the Curfews attacked the Signature End. Chebby won the first corner of the night at Alwyns Lane after Hutchings’ pass was deflected. Rowlatt took this but Pashley headed over.

The hosts took the lead early doors through Nathan Minhas. Bridle spurned an opportunity to level things up almost immediately at the Eden Gate end and Joe Grant dragged a shot off target 60 seconds later.

Both sides exchanged throws in the next passage of play before Rowlatt, who shone at the weekend in his cameo, won the visitors a free kick. Top scorer Bridle had another go 11 minutes in but couldn’t get a decent connection.

Next, Pashley’s straight ball didn’t pick Pattenden and the Chi midfielder had a cross cut out before Bridle, on 16 goals this season in all comps, fired narrowly over the bar. Minhas’ burst of pace gave him some space, although he played a disappointing pass looking for his teammate Berry.

Pattenden then saw his shot blocked in the 18th minute and Minhas picked up a knock. Dunn headed clear a long Curfews’ throw and Eoin Casey was booked for fouling Hutchings at the mid-point.

Chertsey keeper Luke Roberts gathered Bello’s pass towards Pattenden before Hutchings and Chebby hooked up down the left flank, although Bridle’s flick was easy for Richards.

A lovely touch from Rowlatt set him up for a ball that didn’t quite find a marauding Chebby, and Pashley cleared Berry’s delivery as the home side pressed again. Pattenden’s cross/shot wasn’t turned in by Bridle on the half hour mark and Evans comfortably saved a shot by Berry as things swung this way and that.

Then Minhas tried to curl one but Evans denied him easily enough before Darryl Harrison was fouled on the edge of the penalty area and Dunn was booked. Berry was adjudged to have hand balled on 37 but Hutchings’ set-piece got headed away and Evans met the ball before Berry.

With five minutes of the first half to go Pashley beat Minhas and Dunn was fouled by Wayne Ridgely – no yellow card according to referee Adam Steele. A bit of Chuckle Brothers stuff between Bello and Pattenden didn’t work out and Town countered and won a corner which the Lillywhites’ back-line cleared.

Evans claimed a Conor Lee effort without any trouble and on the stroke of half time Chebby could have/should have gone down in the box but he won a corner that came to nothing as Mr Steele blew for the break.

Rowlatt was subbed at the interval for Worthing loanee Burgess and Ridley came off and got replaced by Leo Farruch. Pattenden went down and received some physio treatment after barely a minute and Chebby did Casey but Hutchings’ cross was too deep.

Then Roberts got to it ahead of Bridle on 50 minutes before Hutchings headed the ball out for a Town corner which Chebby hacked away. And it was 2-0 in the 53rd minute when Berry headed home, and Chebby won the visitors a corner that Sweet blazed off target.

A Hutchings’ foul on Lee led to a free kick which Chertsey captain Alex Fisher took, and Evans comfortably saved the consequent header. Next, Isaac Olorunfemi pulled the trigger but it was miles off and Pashley pulled one back for the Sussex side on 63 minutes with a header from a City corner.

Pattenden was beaten to the ball by a defender and Roberts in the 66th minute as Chichester sought an equaliser. Farruch then fired an attempt wide of the mark; Bridle was flagged offside; and Pashley blocked the follow up shot when Hutchings got done.

Bridle couldn’t get his feet right and had an effort saved for a corner on 73. Sweet did well up against Minhas in the 74th minute, and Dunn thought he had won a corner but the ref gave a Curfews’ goal kick. Moments later Pattenden crossed although City couldn’t profit from it before Olly Munt was introduced for Joe Moore.

Sweet tried to find Pattenden on 82 minutes but Roberts gathered and both Bridle and Bello had chances blocked – the second one for a Chi corner. The two teams exchanged set pieces in the following spell and Bridle earned Chichester a corner.

Then it was easier to score then miss for Grant but he somehow missed his second bite at the cherry with two minutes of normal time to go. Hutchings couldn’t keep his shot down in the 89th minute and Clarke replaced Sweet.

The ref added seven minutes of additional time and nice skill from Chebby won Chi a corner that Hutchings delivered for another on the other side. Try as they might Chichester just couldn’t find a leveller as the game drew to a close.

Chichester City: Evans, Bello, Hutchings, Moore, W. Sweet, Pashley, Dunn, Pattenden, Rowlatt, Chebby, Bridle (Munt, Clarke, Burgess).

#1931. Premier League legend David Silva, 40, makes emphatic return to football with man-of-the-match performance - three and a half years after retiring

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:23 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026

David Silva made his mark in his first game since coming out of retirement after scoring on debut in a man-of-the-match display for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin on Saturday.

Last month, the Manchester City icon revealed he was lacing his football boots in a professional sense again for the first time since 2023.

The 40-year-old started for Sha Tin and broke the deadlock against HK Rangers from the penalty spot in the 56th minute.

Silva stepped up and coolly passed the ball into the bottom left-hand corner - sending Hong Kong Rangers goalkeeper Ka-Yu Yip the wrong way.

The playmaker's goal sparked mass celebrations from his team-mates and the fans in the stands - with many taking their phones out of their pockets to record the moment.

However, Silva's debut didn't go as smoothly as planned as the visitors equalised in the 65th minute through Ibrahim Yakubu Nassam.

Some Spanish guy just scored a penalty for Sha Tin#DavidSilva #hkpl #hkfootball pic.twitter.com/JCbiYZEKE0

David Silva scored for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin with this penalty in their 1-1 draw on Saturday

The 40-year-old celebrates with his team-mates after scoring against Hong Kong Rangers

Silva was named man-of-the-match, in what his first competitve match in over three years

With 11 minutes remaining, Silva was then booked before he was substituted in the 84th minute with his side down to 10 men following Maxwell Ansah's 81st-minute red card for a second bookable offence.

Despite failing to take all three points, Silva did collect the man-of-the-match award after the full-time whistle.

Sha Tin currently sit 10th in the Hong Kong Premier League with five points from their opening seven matches. They sit one point and place above bottom-placed Eastern AA, who occupy the sole relegation spot, and 14 points adrift of table-toppers North District.

Silva called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Sociedad.

He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny.

He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012.

Upon joining Sha Tin, ex-Valencia midfielder Silva said in an Instagram video: 'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong.'

Silva will hope to lead his side to victory when they take on Southern District in the Hong Kong League Cup Losers play-offs on Saturday.

It will be the first clash between them in Edinburgh this season and in a communication to their fans, Celtic revealed that they have been given approximately 20 per cent less tickets than is usually the case.

A statement from Celtic read: “We have been informed by Heart of Midlothian FC that we will receive an allocation of 508 tickets for our forthcoming match at Tynecastle Stadium at the end of this month.

“Clearly we are surprised and disappointed at this move, which represents another cut of around 20% on our previous allocation and follows significant reductions across recent years.

Hearts later responded with a statement given to our sister title The Edinburgh Evening News, which explained that the move has been done for segregation purposes.

Celtic pipped Hearts to the Premiership title last season, defeating the Jambos 3-1 at Parkhead on the final day of the season.

The end of the match was marred by a pitch invasion by some Celtic supporters, with fans accosting Hearts players on the field of play. The visiting players left the stadium still in their kit, having not showered or conducting post-match interviews.

Celtic currently lead the Premiership by four points under manager Martin O’Neill, with Hearts under Wouter Vrancken in fourth place, 11 points behind but with a game in hand.

#1923. Inside the insane trophy room of Chelsea legend Branislav Ivanovic: Framed pictures of his 42 goals, a ring from Didier Drogba... and an LED football pitch

Published: 04:50 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 8 November 2026

Legendary Chelsea defender Branislav Ivanovic's insane private trophy room has gone viral after a fan posted a tour of the museum online.

The now 42-year-old made 377 appearances for the Blues during a nine-year stint at the club from 2008 to 2017.

He enjoyed a hugely successful time with the west London side, winning ten trophies and becoming one of the club's most decorated defenders.

As well as winning three Premier League titles he landed three FA Cups,  the League Cup, the Community Shield and the Europa League. He also has a Champions League winners' medal with the Blues, though the Serb did miss out on playing in the 2012 final after famously being told by Geoff Shreeves live on Sky Sports that he was suspended following their win over Barcelona in the semi-final.

Branislav Ivanovic won 10 trophies with Chelsea across nine years with the Blues

The Chelsea legend has built a private trophy room in his hometown of Sremska Mitrovica to rival any other

In a video posted to Instagram a fan from Ivanovic's hometown Sremska Mitrovica explained he was allowed access to the private showroom and documented the breadth of trophies, personal honours and shirts he has collected throughout his illustrious career.

Many of the souvenirs are from his time in Russia with Lokomotiv Moscow and Zenit St Petersburg, as well as those he got at Chelsea.

The private museum holds over hundreds of shirts alone and has an entire wall adorned with shirts just given to him and signed by someone he either played with or played against including the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Neymar and Javier Zanetti.

Most Chelsea fans will remember Ivanovic's most crucial goals such as his winners in the Champions League round of 16 against Napoli and the 2013 Europa League final against Benfica.

And the Serbian appears to have made an effort to immortalise every single one of his club goals by framing and displaying a photo of all 42 from throughout his career.

Amongst other quirky designs, the room has a set of football leg stools for guests to sit on at the bar

Mourinho gets a mention having won the Premier League, Fa Cup and League cup with the Serbian in the 2014-15 season

There is also a replica of every trophy he has won in his career as well and a specialty ring he received as a gift from Didier Drogba after Chelsea's 2012 Champions League triumph.

Ivanovic didn't forget to add some style to the room by installing an LED football pitch to light the room and putting swanky football leg chairs at a fully stocked bar.

He even has a slide solely dedicated to displaying quotes from his former manager Jose Mourinho including the Special One's description of Ivanovic as 'The Perfect One'.

Since leaving Chelsea in 2017 the Serb moved back to Zenit St Petersburg before ending his career back in England with West Brom in 2021.

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 17:39

Viktor Gyokeres has suggested that he has no desire to push for a transfer away from Arsenal.

However, Gyokeres has accumulated just 181 minutes of top-flight football this campaign, with Mikel Arteta showing preference to Kai Havertz.

#1920. Cisse discusses humble beginnings, choosing Milan, Italy call-up, Amorim and amazing form

Alphadjo Cisse has shed some light on his journey to becoming an AC Milan player, as well as what his first few months at the club have been like.

It has been a simply remarkable rise for Cisse, who at the start of 2026 was playing in the second division with Catanzaro, on loan from Hellas Verona. Milan bought him from there but left him with his loan club, before a serious injury needed surgery and ruled him out for the rest of the season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Fast-forwarding to early November, and the 20-year-old is currently the top scorer for the Rossoneri with eight goals, the most recent of which came in Sunday’s 2-1 win over Genoa. There is talk of an imminent renewal already, while Roberto Mancini gave him a senior Italy call-up.

Cisse gave an exclusive interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio in which he touched upon various topics from his upbringing to the brilliant moment he is currently experiencing. MilanNews relayed his words.

“My life changed in my father’s factory. A Verona manager went to meet him at work to beg him to take me to their place. He’d been a worker forever: every day he’d leave work at 5:00pm, and by 5:15 he was already outside our house, calling me and taking me to play soccer.

“I still remember the first time. It was afternoon. He came up to the house and said, ‘Come on, I’ll take you somewhere’. And we went to the pitch. He was the one who instilled in me the passion for soccer, and from that moment on, I’ve never stopped.

“My parents made so many sacrifices to support me on this journey: my mom, when she had days off from work, would come up with me to take me on the bus to practice.”

“My mom is a very demanding mom. But she helps me stay focused and prevent fame from overwhelming me. So everything becomes easier with her. They tell me every day that they’re proud of me, but they also do everything they can to keep me grounded.

“Carlos, Milan’s assistant coach, often tells me this too: ‘ Surround yourself with people who truly love you and who help you stay focused’. I’m sure of this: I carry with me the carefree attitude of the child I was. I play with a smile. It’s hard not to have that in these first few months.”

You have just been called up by the Italian national team for the first time…

“I was on my way to do the pre-match interview against Ferencváros in the Europa League and they stopped me to say, ‘Alpha, they’ve called you up to the national team… the senior team!’ I had the match, I only realised afterwards.

“I want to prove I can compete. The call was in the air, they’d been talking to me about it for days… but this is my big chance. I haven’t had the chance to stop and think about my career. Football moves fast.”

“A few weeks ago, they asked me how much of my potential as a player I’d shown. I said 70%. Can I say that? Maybe I need to lower it a bit… let’s say 40%, because I have so many aspects to improve on, but at the same time, I know who I am and what I’m worth.

“Last season, Aquilani – who was my coach at Catanzaro – told me that ‘if you don’t play at least 10 years in Serie A, I think you’ll have failed’. I took it as a positive motivation, a phrase that pushed me to always do better and believe in what I can do.

“One of my friends in football is Favasuli, I met him just last year in Serie B. We often found ourselves talking… daydreaming. I still remember the day he said to me: ‘Think about when one day we’ll face two great teams’.

“I smiled. ‘It would be great to meet again in Serie A, but maybe it’s a little too late for me, I’m already 23…’ Instead, he made it too: Milan-Napoli will be in December, we’ll see. He was my driver, he drove me to camp. He’s proof that there’s no age to stop feeling young or believing in it, no matter the path.”

Your path has already taken you from Verona to Catanzaro and to Milan…

“In those very months, my life changed again. No longer in my father’s factory. In a matter of days, I had gone from wondering how far I was from Serie A to finding myself facing the most important decision of my career.

“I’ll be honest: I didn’t take that moment very well. When I arrived at Catanzaro, I had only played two five-minute games in Serie A, including against AC Milan. Aquilani and manager Polito really wanted me, they pushed me. It was my first experience away from home.

“In just a few months, I scored a lot, everyone wanted me. And in January, I was practically on a flight to Holland, bound for Rotterdam: to sign with PSV. But then AC Milan came along.”

“My friends’ WhatsApp group exploded: ‘Alpha, is it true?!’ And I was like, ‘Yes guys, yes!’ I didn’t want to make the wrong choice: PSV wanted me right away, while Milan would have let me finish the season in Serie B.

“Two great teams, but Milan… how do you explain that? I was experiencing a mix of emotions; my parents told me to stay calm and that the best was yet to come. We decided this was the right choice. And judging by how things are going, I’d say we were right.”

“The first few times I came to Milanello, I did so to recover from my injury. Milan left me at Catanzaro, yes, but after a few days I got injured. In fact, I had serious doubts: ‘I’m coming to AC Milan after an injury, let’s see how it goes’.

“This is exactly what Amorim spoke to me about as soon as we met. We focused on the injury, and he explained what he expected of me on the pitch. He’s a great guy, and he knows how to deal with us young players. And he knows how to keep me grounded. Even though I’m not someone who likes to let my mind wander.”

You kept a promise after your Europa League hat-trick…

“Even after my hat-trick in the Europa League, I have to say that everything was already clear to me: it was simply confirmation to myself that I can compete at this level. I didn’t see it as a point of arrival, but as a promise kept to the child I was.

“And above all, as a promise to keep. Even though I was coming back from a long injury, even though I’m young and have so many areas to improve, I never had any doubts about my abilities or where I could go. I’m very demanding of myself, just like my mother.”

“Modrić gave me some advice on what I need to improve: I need to read the game better and understand the moments of the match. He’s a great player, a spectacular person, willing to help you learn, and interesting to listen to.

“Even though my idol was very different as a kid: Paul Pogba, when he was at Juventus. We do different things on the pitch, and his haircut certainly didn’t go unnoticed by a kid… maybe I’ll get one in the future! What I appreciated about him was that he made people laugh: that’s what I want to do too.

“I was inspired by the player whose jersey I had as a child: Clarence Seedorf. My mother gave it to me; it was the one I wore on the pitch. So maybe it was just my destiny to come here. Seedorf became an idol at San Siro.

“The place where you feel the grandeur, the pressure, the feeling of playing in a stadium that represents a childhood dream. Being there now is like saying to the child I was: ‘See? You did it’. It’s a huge motivation for me. But I’m carefree enough not to be affected by it.

“When you start playing, you notice it less and you don’t pay attention: it’s easier. The fans are incredibly attached to the team. You notice it not just in Milan, but all over the world. And that’s how you understand where you are. I was really impressed by the organisation here.”

Do you like to play with a certain freedom?

“I’m very carefree when I go on the pitch. Whether it’s playing in Serie B or going to San Siro, I think it’s normal for me. I’m the same person I always am. As a kid, I was obsessed with bicycle kicks. I scored five or six incredible goals… now I avoid them!

“In the Verona youth team, I had a coach, Paolo Sammarco, who shaped the way I play today: he gave me a lot of freedom, helping me understand how I should express myself.”

Is it important for young Italian players to have confidence?

“Italy is full of strong young players, I assure you. It all depends on the opportunities you’re given. Many have emerged in recent months, including me, and I’m sure many more will emerge in the near future.

“When you reach a certain level, you’re amazed: one above all, I was struck by Pisilli, he’s simply amazing. I knew him, but when I played with him, I understood his strength. And I understood my own strength when, in my early years in Verona, I approached the big boys.

“The level was rising, but I continued to have faith, to understand that I could achieve great things if I followed the path I had. That I had something special.”

Your life has changed a lot, are you still the same person?

“My life has changed so much in the past few months, perhaps more than I can even realize. There are moments when I stop and think about how different everything is from just a short while ago. Football is taking me to places I dreamed of, but inside I’m still the same boy.

“But I know what my ambitions are. And perhaps that’s exactly what helps me not lose myself, even when everything changes. I try to enjoy every moment, without forgetting where I started from and all the people who have accompanied me to this point.”

Finally, clear something up: how do you say your name?

“My name is Cisse, without an accent. My name can be read any way, but it’s pronounced ‘Sisse’. I even had to send a voice message to the commentators!”

The 2-1 reversal by the visitors, however, leaves Scotland in an unenviable position in this group. Finishing second is the best Pocognoli can hope for, and that would require at the very least taking four points from North Macedonia and Switzerland in the final two matches.

Last time out, four points on the road was pleasing. The 3-0 defeat by Switzerland - World Cup quarter-finalists, it must be stressed - could be partly explained by an early red card for Jack Hendry. The performance against Slovenia at home raised concerns, though, with Scotland too open, fatigued and meek in the final third.

Pocognoli knows that at the very least in this international fortnight, Scotland must beat North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday. The Balkan nation are toiling, have not taken a point so far and looked bedraggled when Scotland vanquished them. It would breathe some confidence into the team ahead of Monday’s trip to St Gallen, where Scotland will face a Swiss side that may already have top spot sewn up.

Finishing second would require positive results in both fixtures. Doing so would be significant, as it would make Scotland second seeds in next month’s Euro 2028 qualification draw.

What is more feasible is improvement from Scotland. While the team certainly played with more adventure and gumption, there remained a lack of ruthlessness in the final third. Kieron Bowie scored his first goal for his country, but McBurnie remains strike-less after 20 appearances. Perhaps the North Macedonians will be more accommodating.

Pocognoli is able to replenish his forward line with two important members of the Scotland squad for the past few years. Torino striker Che Adams missed out last time due to a muscle injury, but he is fit and firing in Serie A, having scored four goals this season. Often asked to plough a lone furrow under Clarke, it will be fascinating to see how he thrives in a more forward-thinking set-up - and potentially with a partner up top.

Adams’ return is welcomed but there can be no doubt that Pocognoli will be most excited to work with Scott McTominay. The 29-year-old talisman was ruled out of the first camp with a minor heart issue but after a successful operation, he has returned to Napoli and while Gli Azzurri are toiling in mid-table, McTominay has netted five goals and remains front and centre of their best work.

Competition in the midfield area remains fierce. Shoehorning McTominay, John McGinn, Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and Ryan Christie into one team has always been a challenge and will be even harder if Pocognoli decides to stick with two strikers - which he should do against opposition of North Macedonia’s calibre. A combination of Adams and McBurnie in attack seems likely, especially as Bowie has not been starting regularly for Sassuolo.

Gilmour became front and centre of Scotland’s midfield in the last international window and was Scotland’s main source of vertical creativity. McGinn and Ferguson started every game - and both are in good form with their clubs. At Bologna, Ferguson tops the charts in Serie A for distance covered (114.1m), total passes (817) and accurate passes (754). Christie and Bournemouth are flying. These are nice problems to have.

Scotland looked jaded by the second match against Slovenia and while this break is shorter, there is an argument for more rotation. And there will have to be changes in defence, given Welsh and Binks have been forced to withdraw from this squad, replaced by forgotten men Ryan Porteous and David Bates, while Scott McKenna is also absent.

Pocognoli operated with a back three but may be minded to change given the absentees and porousness against stronger opposition. While Porteous has fared well in the States with LA, Graham - often a starter for Stoke City - may be ahead of him in the international pecking order. Kieran Tierney withdrew from the last squad, but is fit this time around and can play as a left-sided centre-half.

Captain Andy Robertson will move level with Sir Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps should he be, as is expected, deployed on the left flank. There is more debate on the other side. Winger Ben Gannon-Doak could give Scotland more oomph in a game they have to win than Aaron Hickey and Nathan Patterson.

There’s even debate with the goalkeeper. Angus Gunn’s status as an untouchable No 1 waned a little on the back of performances last month. Could in-form Falkirk stopper Scott Bain oust him?

Pocognoli has options, that’s for sure. The Tartan Army will want to see Scotland more secure tactically. There needs to be a step forward in this brave new world. And while winning in Switzerland may prove a step too far, landing a first home win under the 39-year-old Belgian feels non-negotiable.

North Macedonia at home was the sort of match Scotland gobbled up in the past. This may be a new regime, but that particular old habit must die hard.
