#1917. To infinity and beyond! Another stunning Diego Gomez strike has Brighton up to SECOND and daring to dream... as Brentford's Igor Thiago is goaded into a red card

Published: 11:08 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 8 November 2026

Onwards and upwards go Brighton. Another victory to send them soaring into second place with only Arsenal above them.

It is a lofty perch for the Seagulls and one more admirable when considering the depths from which they have risen.

Homeless and penniless, on the brink of extinction at the end of the last century they are now daring to dream about the Champions League.

To infinity and beyond. Why not? Fabian Hurzeler’s team have already beaten Arsenal and Manchester City without conceding this season.

The only goals scored against them in the last six Premier League games came at Liverpool, where they lost 2-0 but were not outplayed.

City’s season is mired in uncertainty, awaiting sentence for financial breaches and the other half of the traditional Big Six are so erratic there will likely be scope for interlopers when the prized European tickets are handed out in May.

It is six months away but at this moment in time there are not four teams better than Fabian Hurzeler’s.

Brighton appear fully formed. Delightfully fluent in attack. Creative with zip and imagination and different ways to score goals.

There is a defined style of play. Solid at the back with enough sporting maturity to survive a test of needle, which this became against Brentford after the red card for Igor Thiago’s red card.

Diego Gomez celebrated another memorable strike at the Amex Stadium after his halfway-line stunner in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace

The Bees already trailed to a screamer from the left boot of Diego Gomez and went further behind before half time when Pascal Gross converted a penalty awarded for a shirt pull by Keane Lewis-Potter on Luka Vuskovic.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 6; Costinha 6, Dunk 6, Vuskovic 6, Boscagli 7; Gross 8, Andres 6 (Wieffer 46, ); Gomez 7 (Yalcoue 90+3), Ayari 7 (Hinshelwood 78), De Cuyper 7 (Minteh 82); Kostoulas 6 (Rutter 82)

Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Kadioglu, Svoboda

Bookings: Andres, Boscagli, Wieffer, Dunk

Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher 6; Kayode 5, Ajer 6, Van den Berg 6 (Wilson 70), Lewis-Potter 5 (Diouf 59); Sangare 5 (Jensen 59), Janelt 5, Hickey 5 (Collins 46); Ouattara 4 (Yarmoliuk 46), Thiago 3, Schade 4

Subs not used: Valdimarsson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Gross, the 35-year-old midfielder schemer who walloped his penalty into the top corner in emphatic fashion, embodies the confidence pulsing through this team and his goal closed the contest.

The Bees assembled in the deep looking to minimise damage with an eye on a counterattack or a set piece and maybe hoping the officials would see fit to even it up at 10 against 10.

It didn’t happen. Instead, Brighton controlled the ball. They have had more than 75 per cent of possession across 90 minutes and spent the second half probing around the fringes of the Brentford penalty area.

They registered 20 shots in all but there would be no third goal. And nobody minded. They celebrated the victory and a return to the Amex Stadium after five away games in a row and more than 5,000 miles on the road.

Every substitution made by Hurzeler came as a reminder of their strength and quality.

Kaoru Mitoma, yet to feature this season, is expected back from injury soon after the international break.

The Conference League is not proving a distraction to a squad of such depth and Hurzeler gave fans his permission to dream.

'They should be always excited,' said the Brighton boss. 'That’s our job. They can dream. They can have high expectations, but these are things we can’t control. We played good game but always things we can do better.'

This was Brentford’s second defeat in this Premier League season and they had players sent off in both.

'In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation, antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way,' fumed boss Keith Andrews, referring to Yehor Yarmoliuk’s red card against Liverpool, when the Bees finished the game with nine men.

'We should do better, but the game is in a state now and a place I don’t particularly like. And we’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.'

Chema Andres fouled Thiago, fell to the ground and sprang up to confront the Brazilian, who tried to push him away but caught him with a forearm under the jaw.

Igor Thiago's yellow card was upgraded to red after a VAR intervention

Andres collapsed for a second time. When Michael Oliver gave them a yellow card each it seemed fair, but VAR Stuart Attwell sent the referee to the pitch-side screens for a review.

Oliver studied the slow-motion replays and upgraded it to a red card. Off went Thiago, smiling wryly and shaking his head, dismissed for standing his ground and being goaded into a reaction.

He will miss games against Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.

Opinions of Oliver in the away end did not improve when he gave a penalty for a shirt pull by 5ft 7in Keane Lewis-Potter which somehow sent 6ft 4in Luka Vuskovic somersaulting to the turf.

Vuskovic is already a favourite at the Amex Stadium and it is easy to forget he is only 19. He dominates in the air and reads the game like a seasoned central defender.

And after ten games he is ten points better off than those he left behind at Tottenham.

The Croatia international cannot be looking forward to yet another encounter with England. The two nations meet at Wembley on Thursday. England have put 11 past them in two games this year.

#1916. Tunisia vs Libya - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 11 Nov 2026 17:50, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 17:52

Tunisia and Libya will both look to kickstart their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns with a win when they meet at Stade Taieb Mehiri on Friday.

Both teams are winless from the opening two matchdays, and a defeat for either side could leave them with too much ground to make up at the midway point of the qualifiers.

After qualifying for each of the last 17 AFCON finals - the longest active streak of any nation - Tunisia have arguably been the most underwhelming team of the qualifiers so far, having been held to draws by Uganda and Botswana.

This continues what has been a torrid 2026 for Moin Chaabani’s men, who are now winless in eight matches and have conceded in each of their last seven outings.

A return of just two points from a possible six leaves the Eagles of Carthage, who have topped their qualifying group five times in the last six editions, third in Group H and currently on course to miss out on African football’s showpiece event for the first time since 1992.

However, much could still change for Tunisia over the course of their double-header against Libya, with the sides set to meet again in Tripoli next Thursday after this weekend’s clash.

Having won each of the last four meetings - all in AFCON qualifying - Friday’s hosts will be confident of overcoming their North African rivals in both upcoming encounters and putting themselves in pole position to clinch an AFCON spot.

While Tunisia have been AFCON regulars, Libya have featured at just three tournaments in their history. Their quest for a fourth began on a positive note, coming from two goals down to earn a point against Botswana in their opening qualifier.

Carrying that momentum into their second outing, Youssouph Dabo’s side travelled to Hoima to face Uganda, where they were arguably the better team but left empty-handed after Arnold Vula’s strike on the stroke of half-time.

Since a five-match unbeaten run (W3, D2) between September 4 and November 15 last year, the Mediterranean Knights are now winless in their subsequent five games, with Dabo’s appointment to replace Aliou Cisse yet to deliver the desired impact.

Libya have managed just one victory in their last 13 AFCON qualifiers and now require two wins in quick succession to lift themselves off the bottom of Group H before the final round of matches in March 2027.

Both of Friday’s opponents have struggled defensively, so goals at both ends look likely. Striking first could prove crucial for the visitors, with the hosts having conceded the opening goal in six of their last seven matches.

Libya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Elias Achouri, Ellyes Skhiri, and Hannibal Mejbri are all ruled out through injury and will play no part for Tunisia on Friday.

Hazem Mastouri’s brace against Botswana means he has now scored three goals in his last two international appearances, so he is one to watch.

Midfielder Ferjan Sassi is one appearance away from equalling Radhi Jaidi’s all-time record of 105 for Tunisia and could make history on Friday.

Ezzeddine Al Mariami has been directly involved in each of Libya’s last three goals, making him the visitors' biggest attacking threat at the moment.

Twenty-five-year-old Osama Al Shreimy plays his club football in Tunisia with Club Africain and will be eager to impress against his adopted home nation.

#1914. Cisse like the greats, Amorim surpasses Allegri: All the key stats from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan won their seventh Serie A game of the season on Sunday afternoon, beating a Genoa side that entered the game in great form.

The home crowd at the Marassi were fired up going into this one given Genoa had won four of their last five. However, goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes was exactly what Milan needed to take the ascendancy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson did score inside the final few minutes as Genoa mounted a late surge in the hopes of snatching a point, but the Rossoneri held on to win 2-1 and move back into the top four places in the table.

Looking at the general stats makes for interesting reading. Milan dominated the ball with 62% possession, but Genoa had nearly double the Expected Goals (1.14 to 0.61), even though big chances ended up being even at two apiece.

The Rossoblu also had nearly triple the shots (17 to 6) and shots on target (5 to 2), while the Rossoneri did not win a single corner. It suggests that Ruben Amorim’s side simply took their moments and sat back, though maybe Daniele De Rossi can feel a bit hard done by.

📊 The stats from the win against Genoa. pic.twitter.com/wr1E6cohcZ

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 8, 2026

Alphadjo Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8).

In terms of minutes per goal in Serie A, Cisse leads the way with one every 81 minutes. That puts him ahead of the likes of Donyell Malen (one every 82), Lautaro Martinez (one every 88) and Gustavo Varela (one every 91).

After 13 appearances for Milan, Cisse is level with Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and Alberto Gilardino on 8 goals. Pierino Prati (10) and Mario Balotelli (12) are the only players to record more.

Milan are unbeaten in their last 11 Serie A matches against Genoa (W7, D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

The Diavolo have won each of their last five Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against one team do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven).

Milan have won three and drawn three of their first six away games this season. The Rossoneri have pnly avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

With this victory, AC Milan climbed to 24 points in the standings, two more than the number earned by Massimiliano Allegri’s Milan last season after 11 games. This is also better than Stefano Pioli’s last season, also by two points.

#1911. Spurs transfer news: Pedro Porro admits admiration of Barcelona chief Joan Laporta is "flattering"

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 18:03, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 18:03

Pedro Porro has reaffirmed his commitment to Tottenham Hotspur, despite admitting that he is 'flattered' to have an admirer in Barcelona president Joan Laporta.

The 2026 World Cup winner has recently committed his future to Spurs by signing a new long-term contract.

However, having admitted that he would like to return to La Liga at some point in his career, speculation remains over his future.

Given his status with Spain, it is fair to assume that only Barcelona, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid are potential destinations for the 27-year-old.

Speaking in an interview with SPORT, Porro acknowledged that he was grateful for the "compliment" that had come his way.

When quizzed on his current status, Porro said: "I have a contract with my club and I'm very happy there. I also have to respect that.

"Obviously, that's football: things come up, rumours circulate, but right now I'm focused on the national team and then we'll see."

Nevertheless, when asked specifically on interest from Barcelona, he added: "Yes, of course it's flattering.

"When one of the best clubs in the world is interested in you, or at least that's what they say, it's always a good thing, because it probably means I'm doing my job well. I have to keep going in the same direction."

Porro revealed that he had not been made known about Laporta describing himself as a fan of his, saying: "I hadn't seen it. It's also a compliment on his part.

"As I said before, it's good when, for example, the president of another club, not mine, values ​​my work. It certainly means I'm doing things right."

With a contract in place at the Tottenham Hotspur until 2031, Porro will not be leaving North London anytime soon.

The assumption is that he will reach at least 2028 in the colour of Spurs, then reassess his future after Euro 2028.

A middle ground may be found by all parties, with Porro likely to want to play in La Liga before the latter phase of his career.

And it arrived on the back of an encouraging display in the club's FA Cup blitzing of Marine.

City may have gorged on 11 goals in two resounding Valley Parade cup wins to start getting the Huddersfield Town derby loss out of their system and answer talk that they are goal-shy, but Morgan's poise in the middle was among the key elements.

Boss Michael Duff, who handed debuts to the impressive Zac Hadi, Leeroy Gomes, Gabe Holt and Oliver Hewitt - with Harry Ibbitson making his home bow - said: "It takes time and opportunity. And when the team's been going so well, it's tough to get those opportunities. So all he can do is, when he gets opportunities, do what he's done in the last two games.

Cameron Dawson (calf), George Lapslie (hamstring) are set to be out for up to four weeks, but Josh Neufville should be available for the home derby with Doncaster Rovers on November 21.

Lindsey, who changed his entire starting line-up from last weekend, said: "It wasn't a 4-0 game for me and I was really pleased with lots of it, to be fair.

"We had two young 18-year-old's start the game and I think we finished with three 18-year-old's and a 17-year-old. I'm really proud of those boys.

"There were lots to be really pleased about, but games are won and lost in both boxes.

"We had some good chances, we just didn't put them away and they did."

#1908. Marco Rose's Bournemouth should not have the depth to win this many games domestically and abroad but at Ipswich they showed they can do it the hard way, writes JAMES SHARPE

Published: 11:20 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 8 November 2026

Juggling domestic duties with European adventures should not be as manageable as this for teams like Bournemouth.

Clubs of their size should be creaking under the weight of the extra fixtures. All those games, all that travelling. They have played nine games in a month.

Far bigger outfits have toiled spinning those plates. Remember when Ange Postecoglou stopped bothering about the Premier League entirely just to focus on the Europa League.

And yet here are those brilliant Cherries, three days after a win in Prague in that same competition, making it eight on the bounce with a victory at Ipswich thanks to Evanilson's opener, following goalkeeper Christian Walton's early howler, and an own goal from Leif Davis.

Bournemouth haven't done that since 2013 when they were getting out of League One.

Now, they are seventh in the Premier League, second in the Europa League.

Leif Davies reacts after scoring an own goal to make it 2-0 to Bournemouth

And they're in the League Cup quarter-finals – all while having the squad depth to name Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi on the bench.

Marco Rose's side showed they can also do it the hard way, too, after Jack Clarke's second-half penalty for Ipswich, given for a soft foul on Abdoul Ouattara, provided a far more tense final 15 minutes than anticipated inside a feverish Portman Road where Julio Enciso also twice went close from late free-kicks.

'One goal changed the momentum of the game and that's why I'm much more pleased about the last 20 minutes because we suffered but we did it together,' said Rose.

First James Trafford, now Walton. Bournemouth's win over Leeds last weekend also hinged on a goalkeeping howler, when Trafford's simple pass out from the back was intercepted.

This time Ipswich stalwart Walton took a back pass from Dara O'Shea and decided the best course of action was to try to dummy and turn Evanilson. He failed, of course.

Evanilson rolled the ball into an empty net. That intense Bournemouth press really can do some crazy things to you.

IPSWICH (4-2-3-1): Walton 4; Ouattara 5, Diop 6, O'Shea 6, Davis 5; Florentino 7 (Akpom 85), Palacios 6; Maeda 6 (Fatawu 65, 7), Enciso 7; Philogene 6 (Clarke 54, 7); Emersonn 5 (Flemming 54, 6)

BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 6; Smith 6 (Diakite 79), Hill 7, Silva 7; Truffert 7; Adams 7, Christie 6 (Cook 67, 5); Rayan 6 (Adli 86), Kluivert 6 (Kroupi 68, 6), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 85)

After scoring the opener in Bournemouth's win last weekend, manager Marco Rose told Evanilson that he was becoming a 'real No9'.

That's six goals now in his last seven games but it's his all-round play that's so impressive.

He dropped in and played a beautiful curling through ball into the channel to set Justin Kluivert free down the right.

He collected the loose ball for the second goal.

He made a fine run to latch on to a free-kick over the defence to stab the ball over to James Hill at the back post, who headed over from close range, which would have put him level with Declan Rice as the leading assister in the league too.

'He's so hard-working,' added Rose. 'He does everything out of possession.

'He starts the press, he plays in between the lines, he gives us deep runs.

'But the most important thing is scoring and he understood that he also needs to arrive close to goal if he wants to score.'

If the Tractor Boys are to make their stay in the Premier League a longer one than last time, they cannot afford to keep giving early leads. The mountain is steep enough.

Evanilson's opener was the sixth time Ipswich have conceded inside the first 15 minutes of a league game this season. They are yet to score one that early.

A howler from Ipswich keeper Christian Walton gifted Evanilson the opener

James Hill celebrates Bournemouth's win which lifts them to seventh

It is what will make this defeat especially frustrating for Gary O'Neil against his former club. 'Gary, what's the score?' chimed the travelling fans.

For so much of the contest, Ipswich looked composed and confident on the ball, played with energy and intent and, after they pulled one back, showed how much pressure they can put teams under and how much this place can bounce.

They are a much better side than the one that came up last time but you cannot come out after the break and have Ouattara give the ball straight to Evanilson again inside 30 seconds as he did before Ryan Christie's shot took two deflections and went in.

'Gutted,' said O'Neil. 'To lose a game that you haven't been outclassed is tough to take. We restricted Bournemouth to nothing of their own doing. If you give the ball to the opposition number nine twice, it's going to be difficult.'

#1907. Sky: Ramos involved but has minimal support – the numbers that illustrate Amorim’s point

Some interesting analysis on AC Milan and Goncalo Ramos’ attacking struggles has been provided by the Sky studios.

It was a familiar tale for Ramos during Milan’s 2-1 win over Genoa on Sunday. He was involved but rarely inside the box, then he was selfless instead of ruthless in front of goal when he chose to square for Christian Pulisic to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The worries are starting to grow regarding whether the Portuguese can provide the output required of a number nine that cost €70m. Yet, the Rossoneri have scored 23 goals in 11 league games which suggests goals are coming from elsewhere, sometimes with Ramos’ help.

Sky offered some interesting insight after Sunday’s game. Firstly, they picked out just how involved Ramos actually is with various aspects of Milan’s overall play.

For example, he is first among Serie A strikers for interceptions and recoveries, while he is second for receptions, touches and duels. He is third for passes.

He is first among centre-forwards in the league for touches in the middle third of the field and touches in the opposition half. He is second for fouls committed plus fouls suffered among forwards, with 41.

Sky then shift the focus to the team’s overall play to try and explain why Ramos perhaps isn’t getting the quality service and is having to drop deeper as a result.

They look at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of.

What does this tell us? Well, Amorim’s post match assessment about struggling to get the ball from the defensive third into the final third are true. Milan have a lot of the ball but still struggle to progress it, as the coach told Sky.

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals,” he said.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1906. Boss hopes Lady Luck smiles on Horsham FC as attention turns to FA Trophy tie with Torquay

The Hornets host National League South rivals Torquay United in the FA Trophy second round this Saturday as they look to replicate last season’s run to the quarter-finals.

Horsham have already faced the Gulls this season, drawing 1-1 at Plainmoor on the opening day of the 2026-27 campaign.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Di Paola admitted the Hornets couldn’t have asked for a tougher draw – but the boss hoped a little bit of luck could help Horsham progress.

He told us: “We said when it was drawn it was a tough one but we will approach like we have with every game. We’ll approach it with the right frame of mind.

“I’m desperate to get through. You only have to look at Plymouth Parkway [in the FA Cup] and the draws they’ve had in every round. That’s what you need. I’m not one to blow my own trumpet, but when you do well you do have a bit of luck.

“I’ll always remember the Woking game that got us our first first round [FA Cup appearance in 2021]. They had two or three great chances, Sam Howes made a great save, they missed one at the back post they should have scored, and then with a few minutes to go we scored a free kick that got us into the first round.

“You do need a bit of luck and Plymouth have had a lot of it in terms of draws. They’ve been at home every round – but that’s what you get sometimes. That’s cup football.

“We want to do well in the Trophy like we did last year – it’s good for the finances – but we’re coming up against a team that should make the play-offs comfortably, given the resources they’ve got.

“It’s not an ideal draw but what draw ever is? We would have said Plymouth Parkway was a good draw because they were in the league below, but obviously they were a good side.”

Jimmy Wild is cup-tied for the Trophy tie with Torquay, but the Hornets have no fresh injury concerns.

One player who will no longer feature for Horsham is Archy Taylor, who departed the club on Friday (November 6).

The full-back joined the Hornets ahead of the current season and made a total of 10 appearances.

On Taylor’s departure, Di Paola said: “It’s just unfortunate he’s come up against Lee Harding, who’s one of our best players. He just couldn’t get a foothold in the side.

“With Coxy [George Cox] coming in we have to balance the books, which is perfectly fair. It just got to the point where he wasn’t playing a lot.

“He’s only 22 and he’s probably had two years of setbacks and he just needs to play somewhere and get some football under his belt and get his confidence back. His confidence had gone through the floor because he wasn’t playing, which is common in footballers. He just needs to go and play and enjoy his football somewhere.

“He’s a lovely lad. He saw the writing on the wall and I respect anyone who wants to go and play football. I hate players who are quite happy to sit on the bench or not play.

“Especially younger players, I think money shouldn’t be a factor in your football life when you’re a kid. You should just want to get out and play football while you can because you’re a long time. Fair play to him for wanting to do that. All the best to him.”

#1904. Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Five signings the Red Devils could make in 2027 to transform themselves under Argentine

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 18:13, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 18:18

Manchester United are soon expected to confirm Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach, with Michael Carrick set to be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

An announcement from Man United on the removal of Carrick is likely to arrive on Thursday, with Pochettino leaving his managerial role with the United States in order to take charge of the 20-time English champions.

Man United are expected to at least attempt to add to their squad in January, but the bulk of their business for 2027 will have to wait until the summer.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five signings the Red Devils could make in the middle of next year to hand Pochettino a huge chance of enjoying a successful 2027-28 campaign.

Man United overhauled their midfield during the summer transfer window, bringing in Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, but it would be fair to say that the balance in the middle of the park is still not quite right at this moment in time.

Manuel Ugarte is likely to leave next summer, once he has recovered from a serious knee injury, while there are question marks surrounding Bruno Fernandes' long-term future.

As a result, there is expected to be space in the squad for another midfield arrival, and bringing in Scott from Bournemouth would be a huge statement of intent.

The 23-year-old - valued in the region of £80m by Bournemouth - is also wanted by Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool.

However, Man United should also be firmly in the mix for the England international, who has quickly developed into one of the leading central midfielders in the Premier League.

There is currently widespread speculation surrounding Karl's future at Bayern, with the Germany international potentially being allowed to leave Allianz Arena in 2027.

Karl, 18, has scored three goals and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Vincent Kompany's side during the 2026-27 campaign.

The versatile attacker has represented Bayern on 54 occasions, scoring 12 goals and registering 10 assists, and a recent report claimed that Man United had been 'alerted' to the possibility that the teenager could be available in 2027.

Karl is said to be valued by Bayern in the region of £50m, and he could potentially be a long-term replacement for Fernandes at Old Trafford.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Esposito's future, with Arsenal and Man United believed to be interested in the Italy international.

The 21-year-old has scored four times in 13 appearances for Inter this season, in addition to coming up with two assists, while he has 15 goals and nine assists in 63 appearances for the club in total since breaking into the first team.

The 6ft 3in striker is said to be valued by Inter in the region of £84m, so it would be a major deal for Man United.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are a concern, and it would be some statement from the Red Devils if they were able to win the race for Esposito, who was allegedly scouted by the English giants last weekend.

Man United are long-term admirers of Branthwaite, with the Red Devils making an attempt to sign the centre-back from Everton in the summer of 2024.

It is understood that the Red Devils had at least two offers for the Englishman turned down, but it is possible that their interest could be reignited in 2027.

Branthwaite has made nine appearances for Everton this season, and the 24-year-old is producing high-level performances for the Merseyside outfit.

The Englishman has a contract with Everton until the summer of 2030, but it would be difficult for the Toffees to fight off serious interest from Man United next year.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are both likely to leave Old Trafford in 2027, and it is absolutely vital that the Red Devils boost their defence next summer.

Man United attempted to sign Hall from Newcastle over the summer, but the club were ultimately unable to secure a deal for the England international.

The 22-year-old signed a new contract with the Magpies in September, with his contract at St James' Park due to run until the summer of 2031.

However, it is not impossible to imagine Hall being on the move next summer, with Man United desperate to bring in a new left-back.

Luke Shaw could be released next summer, and Man United need a long-term option in that area of the field, with Hall said to be incredibly keen on a switch to Old Trafford.

#1903. Liverpool played like a team fighting for their manager, but Pierre Sage looks like a dead man walking, writes LEWIS STEELE - as Reds clinch morale-boosting win at sorry Crystal Palace

Published: 11:14 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 13:00 EST, 8 November 2026

By this time of the season, spirited performances mean little if you don't have the results to go with it.

Pierre Sage, who was sacked at Lyon two years ago, knows as much as anyone that this is a results-based business.

And he simply has not had enough results. Despite having Liverpool on the ropes at times here, Crystal Palace failed to land a knockout blow and that could be that for their under-fire manager, who looked like a dead man walking when he trudged off the pitch at full-time with a face like thunder.

Former Lens over-achiever Sage now seems set for a stuffing six weeks before Christmas and though he may curse at the small margins that denied his team a chance of a heavyweight and potential job-saving scalp here, the boss knows two wins in 10 league games is not good enough.

Liverpool, meanwhile, had the width of the crossbar and a throwback performance from goalkeeper Alisson to thank. In contrast to Sage, Andoni Iraola's side showed grit and determination to win when far from their best.

Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak all scored as the Reds put a tough week behind them that saw them lose back-to-back games for the first time in the Iraola era, which prompted a chorus of the old terrace classic 'Poetry in Motion'.

Florian Wirtz scored a rare Liverpool as they won 3-1 at Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Wirtz scored Liverpool's second on 54 minutes as they ran out as 3-1 winners at Selhurst Park

Things are looking ominous for under-pressure Palace manager Pierre Sage after another loss

This performance was hardly William Wordsworth levels of poetry and Liverpool were far from on song during large swathes of this match but when it really mattered, the attackers demonstrated just why the club spent so much money on them.

CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-2-1): Henderson 5; Lerma 6, Richards 6, Disasi 5; Mingueza 6 (Khalali 87), Wharton 5, Timber 6 (Timber 60, 6), Mitchell 6; Kamada 6, Pino 7 (McNeil 87); Larsen 5 (Nketiah 72, 7)

Subs not used: Benitez, Canvot, Chilwell, Doucoure, Hughes

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 9; Araujo 7 (Gomez 90), Jacquet 6, Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 6; Szoboszlai 7 (Nyoni 69, 7), Mac Allister 8; Gakpo 6 (Ngumoha 76) Wirtz 8, Barcola 7 (Munoz 69, 7); Isak 7 (Koumas 90)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, McConnell, Tsimikas

Booked: Araujo, Barcola, Munoz, Mac Allister

Scorers: Mac Allister 40, Wirtz 54, Isak 89

Mac Allister resumed his bemusing role of the team's best aerial threat despite being their smallest player, Wirtz got a goal and assist, while Isak made it eight for the season to continue his prolific streak.

Bradley Barcola, meanwhile, proved what an asset he is despite a wasteful first half.

Those attackers were worthy of praise but no one deserved plaudits more so than goalkeeper, Alisson, who was player of the match in an illustration of Palace's first-half supremacy.

'I'm very pleased with Alisson's performance,' said Iraola. 'He has commanded the box very well and in games here a lot of things are normally happening in the boxes. He has shown the level he has for us. Overall we are getting good results away from home at difficult stadiums.'

The Brazilian is in the last year of his contract but put in his best performance for 18 months, dating back to a 1-0 win at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League knockouts. He will not go on international duty and instead rest up after an injury-hit few years.

He denied Adam Wharton with a glancing header, thwarted Daichi Kamada with a fierce shot and then tipped round Quenten Timber's effort from distance. Palace also rattled the bar through Yeremy Pino in a first half that really should have ended up differently.

Jorgen Strand Larsen also had the ball in the net but was offside.

As it was, though, Liverpool were the team to take their chance when it came after a period of dilly-dallying and playing the wrong ball, guilty again of indecisiveness similar to the flaws shown against Arsenal last weekend and in the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in midweek.

Liverpool led on 40 minutes when Alexis Mac Allister (centre left) scored from close range

The Argentine celebrates after breaking the deadlock for the Reds in the Premier League clash

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing the sack after his side dropped to the bottom of the Premier League.

Palace have won just two of their ten league matches this season, with Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool leaving them at the foot of the league for the first time in nearly nine years.

Sage is expected to lose his job during the international break, with Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank leading the race to replace the French coach.

However, Sage believes his side have been unlucky with results this season and has requested the hierarchy remain patient.

The 47-year-old, who left RC Lens for Palace in the summer to succeed Oliver Glasner, also admitted the Palace squad needs strengthening - perhaps to absolve himself of some blame.

'You can create the links between these two things,' Sage replied when asked whether being bottom of the league heading into the international break could see him sacked.

'But a lot of times I've said we deserved better and it was the case again on Sunday.

'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.

'I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in that, and if it's not the case, they will take a decision.

'I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100% involved in what I have to do.

'We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be okay.'

Mac Allister was the scorer as he continued a fine resurgence this season, with Dominik Szoboszlai the supplier after a week where he too had been criticised. The Hungarian whipped a cross towards Mac Allister, which was glanced past Henderson for 1-0.

The former Brighton player ran straight towards the Palace fans behind the goal and taunted the supporters that were once his rivals on the south coast.

Liverpool weathered another storm at the start of the second half and soon found themselves two up. Barcola, who had left lots to be desired in the first half, swapped wings at the break and made his first attack count.

The Frenchman put the after-burners on and motored down the pitch before feeding Wirtz, who composed himself and passed into the net for 2-0. Iraola praised the run of Isak which took him away from the ball but dragged defenders with him to create space for his colleague.

Isak squandered a one-versus-one chance not long after but was not going to miss another one minutes later, when a blisteringly quick counter-attack was started by Trey Nyoni and ended with Wirtz feeding Isak, who skipped past Chris Richards and finished calmly.

The three goals will delight the hierarchy, with all three of the £100m boys – Isak, Barcola and Wirtz – registering at least one goal or assist apiece, one each in Wirtz's case.

Alexander Isak scored the visitors' third in the 89th-minute with this right-footed finish

Eddie Nketiah pulled one back for Palace from the penalty in second-half stoppage time

This victory would not have been possible, though, without Alisson, now 34 and in the final year of his deal. For all the attacking talent at Iraola's disposal, the Basque will be delighted at his team's defensive determination when under the kosh here as Palace had 10 first-half shots.

Iraola knows his team has flaws and they remain a work-in-progress. But despite a few challenging afternoons, they appear to be heading in the right direction.

The same cannot be said for Sage, whose side pulled one back in stoppage time through an Eddie Nketiah penalty after Milos Kerkez committed a careless foul.

Palace were unlucky in this game but the cold, hard truth is that the recent FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs feel a world away now as they enter the international break rock bottom of the Premier League.

West Ham also won a European trophy in the last five years and look where they ended up — that should set alarm bells ringing that no success lasts for ever and Palace are not too big for relegation.

Nketiah's goal felt like it was too little, too late and the sage advice for Palace supremo Steve Parish might be a reluctant change in the dugout.

With only 5,472 in attendance at Hillsborough on a cold night and no real jeopardy, the match was played in a subdued atmosphere.

#1898. Winning is the only thing that matters to Rangers midfielder Dan Neil as Ibrox club continue to gain momentum in title challenge

Published: 13:52 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:02 EST, 8 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Dan Neil admits he couldn’t care less about how his side go about picking up points as long as the wins keep coming.

The stand-in captain netted the crucial second in Saturday’s hard-fought victory over St Mirren in Paisley after Ryan Naderi had given the visitors a first-half lead from the penalty spot.

It was a result which extended Rangers’ unbeaten run to 12 in all competitions as they continue to build momentum following an unconvincing start to the campaign, and Neil insists that’s the only thing that matters at this stage.

He said: ‘I think every good team just finds a way to win.

‘Obviously, we’d like to win by four or five goals every single week but unfortunately that’s just not football. I do think it’s an area that we can improve on.

‘There’s been too many games this year where maybe we don’t get that second goal and it’s a bit nervy. Teams get a little bit of confidence off that and the momentum shifts.

Dan Neil savours the moment after putting the seal on Rangers' win with the second goal

‘I think it’s definitely something that we can improve on, putting teams to bed when we do go 1-0 up and go 1-0 up early doors when we’re creating chances.

‘But at the same time, finding a way to win is the most important way and whether that’s 1-0 or 5-0, at the end of the day it’s three points.’

While Rangers weren’t quite at their best in Paisley, they did more than enough to halt their poor recent run away from home.

Back-to-back 2-2 draws at Dundee and Hearts last month saw valuable points dropped in what is shaping up to be a tight title race, and Neil was delighted to get back to winning ways ahead of the international break.

‘The last two away results and performances really haven’t been us,’ said the former Sunderland man. ‘It was important that we didn’t have another one of them going into the break and have it lingering over us. Everyone played their part in making it a comfortable result.

‘Coming away from home in any league is tough, but especially this league. It’s important that the mentality of the group is right, which it is, and I think you’ve seen that on Saturday night.

‘It was important to put that hoodoo of those two results behind us and make sure that we win the game. I think there was some good football played for the majority of the game and we also dug in when we had to. That’s credit to every single player in that dressing room.’

‘People are talking about Mauricio Pochettino and it looks like he’s at the front of the queue right now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

#1896. Andorra vs Gibraltar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 18:15

Andorra will conclude their Nations League D campaign on Friday, when they welcome Gibraltar to Estadi de la FAF d'Encamp.

The hosts are last in their three-team group with one point from their three matches so far, whereas the visitors are second with two points from two games.

Andorra were beaten 1-0 by Malta on October 4 in their latest outing in the competition, with their only point coming in a 0-0 stalemate with Gibraltar on September 27.

All three teams in their group will be competing in Nations League C in 2028-29, but while there is no jeopardy for either team on Friday, their placement in group will determine their rankings for the next campaign.

The hosts have only scored one goal in the group so far, though they have conceded just three times in the group stage.

Boss Koldo Alvarez has been in charge of the national team for 16 years, but he has only overseen 13 wins from his 146 games in the dugout, and he has lost 15, drawn five and won just one of his last 21 matches as head coach.

Andorra's performances at home have been poor considering they have been beaten in six of their past seven fixtures when playing as hosts.

Gibraltar are in arguably their best ever period of form given they are undefeated in their last six fixtures in all competitions, winning on three occasions.

The visitors managed to score 11 goals and concede just twice, and they kept four clean sheets in that time.

It should be noted that Los Llanis did play Liechtenstein, Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands and Sao Tome and Principe in those six clashes, with the latter the highest-ranked nation by FIFA at 194th.

Head coach Scott Wiseman will hope to avoid becoming the first manager in his country's history to lose against Andorra, with his side having won two times and settled for two stalemates in four meetings with their hosts.

Gibraltar have been defeated in five of their seven most recent contests on the road, with their only victory in that period a 2-0 success against Liechtenstein on October 5.

Andorra could use a four-man defence featuring central defenders Max Llovera and Ian Bryan Olivera ahead of goalkeeper Iker Alvarez.

Midfielders Ot Remolins Planes and Eric Vales could be rewarded with their 11th and 25th caps for the national team.

In the frontline, it would not be surprising to see forward Albert Rosas partnered by Guillaume Lopez, with the duo having scored five and two goals respectively for the hosts.

As for Gibraltar, it would not be surprising to see Dan Bent, Bernardo Lopes and Julian Valarino form a back three, especially after the trio started in the reverse fixture against their hosts.

Leon Mason and Nicholas Pozo may be used as two third of a midfield three, while Tjay De Barr and Dylan Borge are set to start up front.

Alvarez; Font, Llovera, Olivera, Nicolas; Alaez, Planes, Vales, Rodrigo; Rosas, Lopez

Banda; Bent, Lopes, Valarino; Ronan, Mason, Torrilla, Pozo, Scanlon; De Barr, Borge

Neither side are likely to be at their best considering there is little to play for given all teams will be in Nations League C.

However, with Andorra backed by a home crowd, perhaps the hosts will be able take at least a point against Gibraltar, who have often travelled poorly.

Meanwhile, defender Radinio Balker hopes this season's three-week international break will be the last of its kind, saying it is bad for players. This month reverts to the more normal two-week break.

Balker, who is in the Suriname squad for Thursday's friendly in Lithuania, came home early in the last break to play at Burton Albion, but still felt his time with his country caused the adductor injury he then picked up on his return.

"I wasn't away for the 16 days that my other team-mates had, but it was a long time," he commented. "You're gone from your normal situation where you have your routine and everything.

"I was only gone for eight days, or nine days, I think. To me, that sounds more realistic, because I came back and I think the injury I endured was probably because of all the travel and being away from my normal routine.

"I can only imagine that my team-mates had similar situations back in Suriname when they came back."

The break wreaked havoc with the League On fixture list, with games organised for both weekends, but postponed if clubs had three or more international call-ups. In the first weekend, that caused call-offs for all five Yorkshire teams in the division, who have had to find new dates for those fixtures.

"I would say two weeks or ten days is probably best," said Balker. "I did understand why they did it this year, because they just had the World Cup, of course.

"So I don't think they will do it more often than this, because there was a lot of complaining about it, but, yeah, the two weeks that is coming is probably better, for sure."

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Cape Verde will be looking to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign off the mark when they welcome Liberia to the Estadio Nacional de Cabo Verde in Praia on Friday evening.

The Blue Sharks sit third in Group K after back-to-back defeats to Mali and Rwanda, while the visitors are bottom of the table and also without a point.

Cape Verde have made a disappointing start to the post-World Cup era, losing both of their opening Group K matches under new head coach Humberto Bettencourt.

They were beaten 3-1 by Mali before suffering a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda, in which Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute strike was cancelled out before half-time and the visitors scored again seven minutes into the second half.

Bettencourt, who spent six years as Bubista's assistant, has overseen two defeats in his first two competitive matches, leaving the Blue Sharks winless in their last six games (D3, L3), a run that includes goalless World Cup draws with Spain and Saudi Arabia, a 2-2 draw with Uruguay and a 3-2 round-of-32 defeat to Argentina.

However, their previous meetings with Liberia offer some encouragement, as Cape Verde have won three of the four encounters between the sides, including a 4-1 home victory in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in March 2011.

Liberia, meanwhile, began their qualifying campaign with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali, where Sylvanus Nimely scored their only goal before Rwanda restored their two-goal advantage from the penalty spot in the 44th minute.

The Lone Star then suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Mali, with Martial Tia's 79th-minute strike settling the contest.

Moroccan coach Mohammed Adil Erradi, who took charge of his first competitive match in Kigali, is still waiting for his first victory.

Liberia have won just one of their last eight matches (D2, L5), with that success coming in a 3-1 friendly victory over Sierra Leone in June, while they have scored just once in their two qualifiers, making a trip to Praia a difficult assignment for a side ranked 146th in the world.

Erradi has welcomed back Hammarby Talang striker William Gibson, while Ralph Weah has also earned a place in the 24-man squad.

#1889. South Korean star Kim Min-su has no goals and no assists, but it's no problem for Rangers boss Derek McInnes

Published: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026

Kim Min-su’s stat sheet since making the big-money move to Rangers over the summer should be the kind of thing that makes a manager legitimately wonder if both he and the club have been taken for a ride.

Twelve games, zero goals, zero assists. A rank-rotten return, on the face of it. So why does Derek McInnes not seem even remotely concerned by the whole palaver?

Well, simply put, he has a set of eyes. He, like everyone else, can clearly see that the South Korean is the heartbeat of everything that has been good about Rangers in an attacking sense ever since he was thrown into the team – even if the numbers don’t quite back it up.

It was the same story in yesterday’s hard-fought – but deserved – 2-0 win away at St Mirren.

It was hard to keep track of the number of times Min-su drifted in from the left-hand side to pick up possession with no opposition player within five yards. That’s not luck, it’s intelligence.

There is nobody playing in Scotland’s top flight more adept at taking the ball on the turn and driving into space either.

South Korean Kim Min-su contributes to all that is good about Rangers' attacking work

Min-su made life difficult for St Mirren during Rangers' 2-0 victory over the Paisley side

Dan Neil scores Rangers' second in a win that keeps them within four points of leaders Celtic

St Mirren couldn’t get near him for the majority of the first hour. They aren’t the first side to experience such difficulties, and they won’t be the last.

In full flight, he is a joy to watch operating in that pocket between the opposition midfield and defence.

It’s the bit after that where things start to become a little trickier for the talented 20-year-old.

He squandered a couple of opportunities to open his account here. The first came after playing a neat one-two with James Penrice late in the first half, with the ball sitting up perfectly for him ten yards out to smash home.

The choice to take one touch too many allowed Declan John to clear the danger.

So much of his game is based on instinct. Indeed, it’s a big part of what makes him such captivating viewing. But his decision-making in front of goal needs a lot of work.

Perhaps he’s guilty of overthinking things too much.

His manager certainly thinks so, admitting post-match that he felt Min-su was becoming ‘obsessed’ with registering his first goal for the club. In key moments, that shows.

A heavy touch early in the second period after being played in by Badredine Bouanani – unusually quiet here on the right – once again suggested he is feeling the pressure.

But let’s not forget, he’s essentially a kid trying to find his feet in a new country, and in a league which couldn’t be more different in terms of speed and style from what he was used to in Spain.

That he has actually managed to settle in so seamlessly should be applauded. It can’t have been an easy transition but he has quickly endeared himself to the supporters.

It’s why they are every bit as desperate as the player himself to get the monkey off his back.

They needn’t worry. If he keeps doing what he’s doing, the goals will come. Of that there is no doubt.

Some context has to be attached to his failure to notch an assist too. It’s a misleading stat, given that it depends entirely on someone else putting the ball away when it counts.

Min-su created multiple chances for his team-mates in Paisley, the best of which saw Kevin Kelsy put through on goal. It’s hardly his fault that the big man fluffed his lines. The Venezuelan has been in good form but had a stinker here.

At some point, everything will come together for Min-su. And it’s not as if he didn’t have an impact in both of Rangers’ goals against St Mirren.

It may have gone unnoticed amongst everything else, but he absolutely busted a gut to get himself into the box in the build-up to Dan Neil’s deflected strike which sealed the points on 61 minutes. That willingness to put the hard yards in off the ball is every bit as impressive as his ability on it.

And it was his pass to Penrice which led to the full-back being clipped by Samuel Ramos inside the box to give Rangers the opportunity to go ahead from the penalty spot early in the first half.

In truth, they may have been a little fortunate to do so. Put it this way, had referee Nick Walsh not given it, there’s not a chance in hell that VAR would have got involved.

Ryan Naderi stepped up to slot into the bottom corner to take his tally to nine for the season in all competitions.

It says a lot about where Naderi's head is that he had the confidence to do so, especially after blowing a great chance from six yards out only moments before. The German-born Czech international is a changed man, all right.

Speaking of confidence, there is no shortage of it at the other end of the park either. At times, the defensive pairing of Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez look like they’re playing five-a-sides.

It’s usually the latter who throws in the odd lapse of concentration to add some peril to proceedings, but yesterday it was the normally dependable Makhanya’s turn to give his manager a few hairy moments. Thankfully for the South African, St Mirren couldn’t take advantage.

Craig McLeish’s men could have no complaints over the final result but could have made things interesting late on had either Eseosa Sule or Calvin Ramsay finished from close range.

It’s now just one win in nine for the Buddies, who – much like last season – just can’t seem to put the ball in the back of the net consistently. That problem plagued them so much that they ended up in the relegation play-off spot last year.

McLeish has done an excellent job since taking over from Stephen Robinson. A far better one than anyone could have possibly predicted. He has changed the style of this team completely in a very short space of time and so you have to trust he will be able to find a solution to their goalscoring issues too.

Rangers might be 13 points better off but they head into the international break also in search of that perfect balance.

When they’re on it, they’re very good. But they are still not commanding games from start to finish with any sort of regularity.

They won’t necessarily have to be pleasing on the eye to end up with their hands on the Premiership trophy come May. Celtic’s triumph last season proved that.

The Rangers supporters will gladly put up with imperfect displays for the next six months if that’s going to be the end result.

And if the likes of Min-su can hit the goal trail sometime soon, there’s a decent chance that’s exactly how things will play out.

#1888. Harry Kane for England - the only non-negotiable in Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions squad

For really the first time in his international career, Jordan Pickford has genuine competition for his place as the first-choice goalkeeper, and Leeds United's James Trafford will be hoping for the chance to ramp it up with an appearance either at home to Croatia on Thursday, or in Spain on Sunday. One more cap seems likely, two feels like a push.

But his club-mate Dominic Calvert-Lewin just has to accept he was born at the wrong time – anyone who wants to be England's centre-forward in this era can forget about it unless their name happens to be Harry Edward Kane.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tuchel has already confirmed the 33-year-old will be leading his team out at Wembley – anything else would be cruel.

Getting Kane to miss internationals is a tough job in itself. The number of dead rubbers or easy victories he has featured in is very high but no one should criticise him for being hungry to wear the Three Lions, or even to add to a prodigious goal tally which currently stands at 91.

Even putting him on the bench against the team he scored twice against in October's astonishing 7-0 away win with only a point needed to qualify for the quarter-finals would be an act of cruelty.

For starters: Thursday is the night Kane will be presented with the Ballon d'Or as the best player in Europe – and by extension the world – in the season just gone. It will also be the night he breaks Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps, a record he set in 1989 and extended over the next year.

Yes, internationals are more ten-a-penny than in Shilton's day with competitions like the Nations League springing up and FIFA's greed expanding World Cups beyond what is sensible.

But Wayne Rooney, David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Ashley Cole and Frank Lampard all made it to three figures this century without any going past a goalkeeper who might have played more often had he not been part of a Pickford/Trafford-style rotation with Ray Clemence early in his England career.

And to those of us of a certain age, 49 goals felt like the glass ceiling for England players.

Now it is hard to know where Kane will stop. A ton feels likely.

Bobby Charlton hit his 49th goal in his 101st appearance, in 1970, but could not bring up his half-century in five more caps.

Gary Lineker looked a cert for 50 at one stage, but got stuck in the mud when Graham Taylor foolishly lost faith with him in 1992, missing a penalty for 49 in what proved to be his final appearance, then being controversially substituted for Alan Smith in a European Championship defeat to hosts Sweden.

Alan Shearer only made it to 30 before his international career came to a premature end but when Michael Owen burst onto the scene as an 18-year-old, the record looked under threat again. His time with England fizzled out too, hamstring injuries cutting the country's last Ballon d'Or winner short at 89 caps and 40 goals by the age of 28.

Finally, in 2015, 29-year-old Rooney made it to 50 on the night Kane got his third goal. Thirteen more caps reaped just three more.

Kane has obliterated that, and looks a far more complete player than even then one who set a new record with his 54th goal in 2023.

Then he was a Tottenham Hotspur player, a brilliant No 9, but since moving to Bayern Munich he has developed into an exceptional "false nine" – spending as much time in midfield as up front, and even helping out defensively. He is one of the best midfielders around.

Kane was edging in that direction in his late 20s, but his time in Germany has taken him to a new level.

“I actually don't see a better player, but I see a player that believes he can win,” argued Gareth Southgate, the manager who took him to two European Championship finals and 98 caps. “That's happened to him in the last month alone would have given him another boost of confidence.

“If you sit there and you think: 'My peers, experts, the world has voted me as the best player in the world,' my goodness, how good is that going to make you feel when you've been a player that people said can't even make it as a professional?”

Like Rooney, Kane could extend his career by dropping deeper on the field, a chink of light for those centre-forwards, like Sheffield-born Calvert-Lewin craving a look-in.

His recently-signed new Bayern contract is due to keep him playing for almost three more years. At the rate he has been winning them lately, that would be 36 more caps.

The lessons of Lineker, Shearer, Owen and Rooney is that the end can come abruptly and unexpectedly. Despite what his hairline might have you believe, Charlton was only 32 when he retired.

Whether he makes it to 100 goals or not, Kane is a special talent England should be forever grateful for.

By Joshua Cole | 11 Nov 2026 18:45

Morocco will be looking to maintain their perfect start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they welcome Niger to the Mohammed V Stadium in Casablanca on Friday.

The Atlas Lions have collected six points from their opening two Group A matches and sit top of the table after beating Gabon and Lesotho, while the visitors are third with three points, having won one and lost one of their opening two qualifiers.

Morocco have made an impressive start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, winning both of their opening Group A matches against Gabon and Lesotho by identical 2-0 scorelines.

The Atlas Lions have scored four goals without conceding in the qualifiers, underlining their defensive organisation, while they have now kept clean sheets in three of their last four competitive matches.

Mohamed Ouahbi's side have since returned to action, playing out a 1-1 friendly draw with Mali in October, with Abdessamad Ezzalzouli scoring from the penalty spot in the first half before Gaoussou Diarra restored parity for the opposition.

Niger, meanwhile, have struggled to build on their encouraging start to the qualifying campaign, opening with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho before suffering a 2-0 defeat against Gabon.

The Menas followed that loss with another 2-0 defeat, this time against Algeria in a friendly last month, leaving them with three losses from their last four matches across all competitions.

Their victory over Lesotho remains their only triumph in their last nine matches, a run that has also produced five defeats and three draws.

Responding to a whirlwind of rumours, Zubimendi told Marca: ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Asked whether his current predicament has come as a surprise, Zubimendi revealed Arteta had been totally transparent at the season’s outset and outlined the role he envisaged for a player he fought so hard to sign.

He said:  ‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.’

He added:  ‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Alexis Saelemaekers, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze and Strahinja Pavlovic were all out for the match at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, with the Serbian centre-back being the latest to enter the treatment room.

In today’s edition of Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews), Ordine analysed Milan’s win at the Marassi. He spoke about how the injury situation has forced Amorim to make certain choices, ones that lay everything bare in view of a potentially important winter transfer window.

“Having also lost Pavlovic, who is one of the most consistent players and the most ‘applied’ in training, they had to improvise Diawara at centre-back and even Musah at left-back,” he said.

“And for those who say the lack of confidence in Estupiñan on this occasion was deserved (he came on with just minutes to go and managed to provoke a free kick at the end of injury time that could have proved fatal), some explanation for the failure to use Bartesaghi would be worth seeking.

“Not only that. Later on, when it became clear that the fatigue accumulated on Thursday against the Hungarians had crushed Milan in the final 20-30 metres, Terracciano emerged from the bench as second centre-back on the left, a right-footed player who has only had a few poor performances so far.

“This is essentially a message to the owners, who have already promised to intervene in the January transfer window to fill the gaps. The point is precisely this: until then, the Portuguese coach must continue with his current strength.

“Of course, after the break, he may be able to recover some of the injured players (Tomori, Pavlovic, Loftus Cheek, perhaps Gabbia), but certainly not Saelemakers and Chekwueze, who will be ready between February and March.

“For this reason, the strengthening plan must unravel another knot that has remained tangled for now: that of Ramos’s deputy. The Portuguese, who yesterday drew applause for his generous assist to Pulisic in the penalty area, seems doomed to play every game, and to the very end, because Camarda is only called upon in rare circumstances.

“Here too, as in the case of Estupiñan, who was not sold, acknowledging the error of judgment made in the summer is a sign of intelligence!”

#1882. Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s replacement

Manchester United are close to rubber stamping a deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s successor ahead of making a final decision on the future of their current head coach.

The Red Devils are languishing in the relegation zone after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which is expected to represent Carrick’s final game at the helm, despite an injury-time comeback which yielded an unlikely point.

Carrick currently remains in limbo and attended United’s training ground on Wednesday morning with club executives set to discuss his future at a meeting in Monaco.

The 45-year-old was photographed driving into the club’s Carrington base this morning, but his fate is set to be determined at a meeting 800 miles away, where co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe will confer with United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

According to the Athletic, United’s key decision makers held talks on Tuesday and settled on Mauricio Pochettino as the candidate best qualified to lead the club out of the almost unprecedented mess it finds itself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager signed a contract with US Soccer through to 2030 just three months ago, and is currently preparing the American national side for CONCACAF Nations League matches against Haiti in the November international break.

The former Argentina international has held talks with United in the past and is keen on the job this time, but hefty compensation would be due to US Soccer.

United are understood to have been in contact with Pochettino’s representatives and although personal terms are unlikely to be an issue, the 54-year-old’s exit clause of £7.4million would need to be paid in full.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired, while ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann were linked a fortnight ago when United seriously considered replacing Carrick.

Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away.

‘It’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events,’ Carrick said. ‘But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

United return to action with a Premier League trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1879. Arsenal battle Real Madrid and PSG for £44m-rated Borussia Dortmund wonderkid

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 20:07, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 20:08

Arsenal are reportedly among three European heavyweights monitoring Borussia Dortmund defender Joane Gadou, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain also interested in the highly rated French teenager.

The 19-year-old has quickly established himself in the Bundesliga following his summer move from Red Bull Salzburg, attracting attention from some of Europe's biggest clubs after an impressive start to his Dortmund career.

According to German outlet Fussball News, citing transfer journalist Ekrem Konur, Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG have been following Gadou's development closely and have sent scouts to watch him in action.

Dortmund are reluctant to lose the defender just months after signing him, although offers in the region of €40m to €50m (£35m to £44m) could reportedly persuade the German club to reconsider their position.

No formal asking price has been announced, and there is currently no indication that any of the interested clubs have submitted an offer.

A January transfer is considered highly unlikely, with the summer of 2027 potentially providing a more realistic opportunity for the player's admirers.

Gadou has made a rapid impression at Dortmund, having started 12 of his 15 appearances across all competitions during the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Frenchman has become a regular member of Niko Kovac's defensive unit, competing alongside established players such as Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton.

Standing at 1.95 metres, Gadou combines an imposing physical presence with considerable pace and an ability to contribute to his team's build-up play.

His versatility has also been evident, with the teenager capable of operating on the right of a back three or filling in at right-back when required.

Those qualities have reportedly attracted scouts from Arsenal, Real Madrid and PSG, who are understood to have watched him during Dortmund's encounters with Real Betis and Bayern Munich.

For Arsenal, Gadou is already a familiar opponent.

The defender scored against the Gunners during the Emirates Cup in August, finding the net in the second half as Dortmund secured a 3-2 pre-season victory in north London.

That appearance provided an early opportunity for the Premier League champions to assess the youngster at close quarters, although there is no evidence that it directly prompted their reported transfer interest.

Gadou's development has been particularly rapid considering that he was still part of PSG's academy little more than two years ago.

He left the French champions for Salzburg in September 2024 without making a senior appearance in Paris, subsequently establishing himself in Austria before earning a move to Dortmund in May 2026.

The Bundesliga club reportedly paid approximately €19.5m (£17m) for his services, with further bonuses potentially increasing the overall fee.

Dortmund's sporting director Lars Ricken made clear at the time that the club had followed Gadou since his PSG days and expected him to play an important role immediately.

The French youth international has justified that confidence with his early performances, and his progress now appears to have attracted renewed attention from his former club.

Despite the growing interest, Dortmund are under no immediate pressure to negotiate Gadou's departure.

The defender signed a five-year contract upon his arrival from Salzburg, keeping him at Signal Iduna Park until June 2031.

That long-term agreement places the German club in a strong position should Arsenal, Real Madrid or PSG decide to formalise their interest.

According to Fussball News, bids approaching €40m to €50m could be required before Dortmund would consider changing their stance.

However, that figure represents a reported potential negotiating range rather than an official valuation communicated by the club.

Gadou's estimated market value currently stands at approximately €28m (£24.5m), highlighting the premium Dortmund could seek for a player who has already established himself in their first-team plans.

The Bundesliga side are also understood to have little appetite for selling the Frenchman during the January transfer window.

For PSG, a future move would represent an opportunity to bring back a player developed in their academy, although they would now face a substantial financial commitment to secure his return.

Arsenal and Real Madrid, meanwhile, are being linked with a defender whose early performances suggest that his reputation could continue to grow before next summer.

Much will depend on whether any of the three clubs progress beyond their reported scouting interest.

For now, Gadou remains an important part of Dortmund's plans, and his lengthy contract gives the German side considerable control over any potential transfer negotiations.

#1878. Barnsley FC boss on Makenzie Kirk, Daniel Johnson plus updates on Conor O'Riordan and Ben Hamed Toure

After thumping the Shots 7-2 to book their place in round two of the cup - and secure their first victory in 12 matches in all competitions - the Reds backed up with a 5-2 success in their final Trophy group game against the Latics.

The game saw Makenzie Kirk grab a brace - his first goals for the club at Oakwell - while Daniel Johnson and Luke Alker scored their maiden goals for the club.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Stendel's side will complete a transformational week if they pick up three points at fellow League One strugglers Wigan on Saturday. Barnsley are winless in eight league matches since September 2.

Asked about a momentum shift, Stendel, whose side are unbeaten in their last three matches in all competitions, said: "I think it started a little bit earlier with the game against Oxford, I think. I can see it last week - in the training week.

"On Saturday, in the FA Cup game, I think we were really focused from the first moment. We scored the goals, we defended well for a long time. It was similar (on Wednesday versus Oldham), the start was exactly the same and we scored also three goals.

"It was important and after the game we keep only the positive things at the moment. That means we scored five goals, we won the game again and we had some positive situations in defence and offence. I think a positive mindset is really important for us after this long time we haven't won a game.

"Some players get the confidence that they can score. On Wednesday, it was Makenzie Kirk who scored two goals, I think it's important for him.

"He's a striker, he has this feeling he can do it in a game. Our goal was to play a good game, win the game and take a lot of positive things with us for Saturday. Especially in the first half we did really well. In the second half we lost 20 minutes of control, but in the end we came back and scored two goals.

"I think it was a good night for us and we're really confident at the moment."

Earmarking praise for Johnson, who has started alongside Luca Connell in the midfield in the Reds' big two wins at Oakwell, Stendel continued: "We have two really good experienced players on the pitch who control our game, who decide when we play quick (and) when we keep the ball. Then you can see how important a player like them is for our game.

"I'm happy that DJ played again. It was the reason we wanted, that he played more time with Luca together and that he can score a goal was also good for him."

The Reds have yet to decide whether Conor O'Riordan, who has missed out in the last few weeks with a shoulder issue, will require surgery. Stendel added: "It's a good question. It's a question of if he tries to do it without a surgery. (If he does), it doesn't matter, he needs also a little bit of time (absent), then maybe he is back earlier. But the last (final) decision is not his at the moment. But in the next two games I think he is not ready to play.

"It's especially hard in our situation hard when (Jack) Shepherd is suspended (on Saturday). You can see how many players we have for some positions. But the players that played did it well (this week) and I'm positive that we can do it on Saturday again."

Ben Hamed Toure is due back in training today following compassionate leave.

Stendel said: "We expect him back this week. Normally he is back (on Thursday) and then we have a look again. But then he has not trained five weeks with the team.

"I think it's not so easy to say he is ready to play on Saturday. But when he is back, we have to look how he feels, how is his mood at the moment. And then we talk with him and we find a solution.

"Maybe not for Saturday, but I hope for the next week."

Stendel confirmed that Jono Bland has been training with the under-21s due to a disciplinary issue, but could be back in the first-team fold this weekend.

The Reds chief commented: "At the moment he is still training with 21s. But when he trains well and I have a talk this week with him, maybe he is back in the next time."
